exact_project_or_supplier_declaration_in.name: TauCeti.IsEilenbergMacLaneSpaceOne
exact_project_or_supplier_declaration_in.statement: def IsEilenbergMacLaneSpaceOne (G : Type u) [Group G] (X : Type v) [TopologicalSpace X] (x : X) : Prop := IsAspherical X x ∧ Nonempty (FundamentalGroup X x ≃* G)

abbrev Artin (M : CoxeterMatrix S) := PresentedGroup (braidRelators M)

def generator (M : CoxeterMatrix S) (s : S) : Artin M := PresentedGroup.of s

def coxeterParabolic (M : CoxeterMatrix S) (T : Set S) : Subgroup M.Group :=
  Subgroup.closure (M.simple '' T)

def IsSpherical (M : CoxeterMatrix S) (T : Set S) : Prop :=
  Finite (coxeterParabolic M T)

abbrev SphericalType (M : CoxeterMatrix S) := {T : Set S // IsSpherical M T}

abbrev LiftedCell (M : CoxeterMatrix S) := Artin M × SphericalType M

def wordArtin (M : CoxeterMatrix S) (w : List S) : Artin M :=
  (w.map (generator M)).prod

def wordCoxeter (M : CoxeterMatrix S) (w : List S) : M.Group :=
  (w.map M.simple).prod

def LiftedFace (M : CoxeterMatrix S) (a b : LiftedCell M) : Prop :=
  a.2.1 ⊆ b.2.1 ∧ ∃ w : List S,
    (∀ s ∈ w, s ∈ b.2.1) ∧
    M.toCoxeterSystem.length (wordCoxeter M w) = w.length ∧
    (∀ v : coxeterParabolic M a.2.1,
      M.toCoxeterSystem.length (wordCoxeter M w) ≤
        M.toCoxeterSystem.length (wordCoxeter M w * v)) ∧
    a.1 = b.1 * wordArtin M w

instance (M : CoxeterMatrix S) : Preorder (LiftedCell M) where
  le := Relation.ReflTransGen (LiftedFace M)
  le_refl _ := Relation.ReflTransGen.refl
  le_trans _ _ _ := Relation.ReflTransGen.trans

noncomputable def SalvettiCover (M : CoxeterMatrix S) : TopCat :=
  SSet.toTop.obj (CategoryTheory.nerve (LiftedCell M))

# External Lean prerequisite search for the Lemma 2.8 kernel milestone

Research date: 2026-11-14. Scope: the generalized kernel theorem in
`formalizations/artin-normalisers/`, as specified in `PLAN.md`; no external
proof has been imported or copied, and no project proof was edited in this
search.

## Decision

No additional external prerequisite was found that should be added to this
milestone. The relevant normalizer/quotient foundations are already in the
pinned mathlib. The external projects below contain related constructions,
but their inspected declarations either specialize to a different mathematical
problem or simply wrap existing mathlib results. Adding them would create
version and dependency work without supplying a missing proof.

This is a bounded search result, not a claim that no equivalent theorem exists
anywhere on GitHub. No external proof is accepted as formally verified here:
the rejected candidates were not compiled, their transitive axioms were not
audited, and their kernel declarations were not replayed. Source inspection,
README claims, CI badges, and `#check` would not suffice for acceptance.

## Baseline and exact missing step

Read the repository's `CLAUDE.md` and `README.md`, the complete local
`research/lean-lemma28/PLAN.md`, and the three current proof modules
`NormalizerMap.lean`, `QuotientMap.lean`, and `Kernel.lean` before searching.
The package pins Lean `v4.36.0-rc2` and mathlib
`65d730f7150f21fdfa32f3e73a3f549c1f96a0e9`.

The target has arbitrary groups, arbitrary `f : G →* H`, and arbitrary
`A : Subgroup G`. It identifies the kernel of the map
`N_G(A)/A → N_H(A.map f)/(A.map f)` with the quotient image of
`ker f ∩ N_G(A)`, and provides representatives in `ker f`. It requires no
surjectivity hypothesis and no finite-index, matrix, modular, or Coxeter data.

At the pinned mathlib revision:

- [`Subgroup.le_normalizer_map`](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/65d730f7150f21fdfa32f3e73a3f549c1f96a0e9/Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Subgroup/Basic.lean#L477)
  states `(normalizer A).map f ≤ normalizer (A.map f)`.
- [`Subgroup.normal_in_normalizer`](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/65d730f7150f21fdfa32f3e73a3f549c1f96a0e9/Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Subgroup/Basic.lean#L508)
  supplies normality of `A.subgroupOf (normalizer A)`.
- [`QuotientGroup.ker_map`](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/65d730f7150f21fdfa32f3e73a3f549c1f96a0e9/Mathlib/GroupTheory/QuotientGroup/Defs.lean#L333)
  states, for normal `N ≤ G`, normal `M ≤ H`, and
  `h : N ≤ M.comap f`,
  `(QuotientGroup.map N M f h).ker = (M.comap f).map (QuotientGroup.mk' N)`.

Thus even the general induced-quotient kernel supplier is present already.
For the current problem, instantiate its ambient groups with the two
normalizers and its homomorphism with `normalizerMap f A`. The remaining
identification is the elementary adjustment of a representative `g` by
`a⁻¹`, choosing `a ∈ A` with `f a = f g`. It is precisely the local
`quotientMap_mem_ker_iff` argument. A candidate would be useful if it supplied
this exact general identification without extra assumptions or substantial
translation overhead. None inspected did.

These baseline declarations were read in the actual local pinned mathlib
source, not inferred from current online documentation. Their compilation,
axiom audit, and kernel replay belong to the root package verification; this
search does not independently certify that verification.

## F-Najman/normalizer-lean

Repository: [normalizer-lean](https://github.com/F-Najman/normalizer-lean).
Inspected checkout SHA: `1f4c27ec11da475383f69e6f82e2837a0cb54fd0`.
This is Lean 4, pinned to `leanprover/lean4:v4.35.0-rc3`; its manifest fixes
mathlib to `c55e6e786f49471c72fbddbec5415808896aec1e` (input tag
`v4.35.0-rc3`). The repository's `LICENSE` is Apache-2.0. No code was copied.

Inspected the normalizer/quotient definitions, `B0.lean`'s map and kernel
argument, `GenMain.lean`'s corresponding general congruence-subgroup
constructions, and search matches across the project's Lean sources.

Relevant exact declarations/conclusions:

1. [`NormalizerLean.BG`](https://github.com/F-Najman/normalizer-lean/blob/1f4c27ec11da475383f69e6f82e2837a0cb54fd0/NormalizerLean/Defs.lean#L247)
   abbreviates `NormG Γ ⧸ Γ.subgroupOf (NormG Γ)` for
   `Γ : Subgroup SL(2, ℝ)`, with `NormG Γ` abbreviating its normalizer.
   Its following normality instance is exactly
   `Subgroup.normal_in_normalizer`. This could package the codomain quotient
   only after specializing our arbitrary groups to real special linear
   groups; its entire useful content is already in mathlib.

2. [`NormalizerLean.B0_equiv'`](https://github.com/F-Najman/normalizer-lean/blob/1f4c27ec11da475383f69e6f82e2837a0cb54fd0/NormalizerDelta/B0.lean#L334)
   has parameters `(N : ℕ) [NeZero N]` and concludes

   ```lean
   ∃ φ : Norm0Q N →* B N, Function.Surjective φ ∧
     φ.ker = (Gamma0Q N ⊔ Subgroup.center (GLPos (Fin 2) ℚ)).subgroupOf (Norm0Q N) ∧
     ∀ g : Norm0Q N, (φ g).IsClassOf (normSL g)
   ```
   Here `phi0` is the composition of a quotient projection with `psi0`,
   which restricts determinant normalization of positive rational matrices
   into `SL(2, ℝ)`. Its source is a normalizer, not a normalizer quotient.
   Its kernel is a congruence subgroup joined with scalar matrices; it is
   not the arbitrary-homomorphism kernel statement needed here. Its kernel
   proof uses `QuotientGroup.eq_one_iff` and a specialized matrix-membership
   theorem. The quotient API it uses is already in mathlib.

3. [`NormalizerLean.BQ_equiv_BG'`](https://github.com/F-Najman/normalizer-lean/blob/1f4c27ec11da475383f69e6f82e2837a0cb54fd0/NormalizerDelta/GenMain.lean#L139)
   assumes `{N : ℕ}`, `hN0 : NeZero N`,
   `{Γ : Subgroup SL(2, ℤ)}`, `Γ(N) ≤ Γ`, and `-1 ∈ Γ`. It concludes the
   existence of a surjective
   `φ : NormGQ (Γ.map toGLPosQ) →* BG (toR Γ)` whose kernel is
   `(Γ.map toGLPosQ ⊔ Subgroup.center (GLPos (Fin 2) ℚ)).subgroupOf
   (NormGQ (Γ.map toGLPosQ))`, together with the representative formula
   `(φ g).IsClassOf (normSL g)`. This extends the preceding matrix result,
   not the arbitrary groups or arbitrary homomorphism in our theorem.

4. [`NormalizerLean.BG_GammaH_equiv'`](https://github.com/F-Najman/normalizer-lean/blob/1f4c27ec11da475383f69e6f82e2837a0cb54fd0/NormalizerDelta/GenMain.lean#L60)
   assumes `{N : ℕ} [NeZero N]`, `{H : Subgroup SL(2, ZMod N)}`, and

   ```lean
   ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → p ∣ N →
     ¬ IsBorelMod H p ∨ IsSplitMod H (p ^ N.factorization p)
   ```
   and concludes the existence of a multiplicative equivalence
   `BG (toR (GammaH N H)) ≃* QH H` with its reduction-modulo-`N`
   representative formula. Here `QH H = NormH H ⧸ H.subgroupOf (NormH H)`.
   Its proof computes a specialized map's kernel and invokes mathlib's
   `quotientMulEquivOfEq` and `quotientKerEquivOfSurjective`. It does not
   expose a reusable generic kernel-image lemma.

Direct-use decision: reject as a dependency for this milestone. These are
substantive modular-curve theorems, but no instantiation yields our arbitrary
groups/homomorphism, and their generic quotient constructions duplicate
existing mathlib. No compilation is warranted merely to confirm a result we
would not use. Formal correctness remains unverified by this search. The
repository's advertised theorem count/no-`sorry`/axiom claims were not used as
evidence. Its `Challenge` targets deliberately contain holes according to
`lakefile.toml`; those statement fixtures must not be confused with proofs.

## Arthur742Ramos/GraphCoveringTheory

Repository: [GraphCoveringTheory](https://github.com/Arthur742Ramos/GraphCoveringTheory).
Inspected checkout SHA: `c918a72c5170503c98fd66a0f3116b7bfcd1250c`.
Lean `v4.32.0`; mathlib manifest SHA
`81a5d257c8e410db227a6665ed08f64fea08e997` (input `v4.32.0`).
Repository license: Apache-2.0.

Read the complete
[`GraphCoveringTheory/Deck.lean`](https://github.com/Arthur742Ramos/GraphCoveringTheory/blob/c918a72c5170503c98fd66a0f3116b7bfcd1250c/GraphCoveringTheory/Deck.lean).
Its exact endpoint is the noncomputable definition
`GraphCoveringTheory.quotientDeckGroupEquiv (G : Type u) [Group G]
(H : Subgroup G) [H.Normal] [Fintype (G ⧸ H)] :
G ⧸ H ≃* SchreierDeckGroup G H`, with a finite-index variant.
It identifies automorphisms of a finite regular Schreier action with a group
quotient; supporting lemmas prove injectivity and surjectivity of a right
translation action. Imports are `GraphCoveringTheory.IndexFormula` and
`Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Action.Concrete`.

Direct-use decision: reject. It has a normality and finite-quotient setting,
no ambient homomorphism `f`, no map between two normalizer quotients, and no
required kernel-image equality. Specializing it to the subgroup in a
normalizer would additionally require finite index, absent in our statement,
and would produce an unrelated deck-group equivalence. Formal correctness
was not independently checked; no build/audit/replay was run.

## SauersML/group-approximation

Repository: [group-approximation](https://github.com/SauersML/group-approximation).
Inspected checkout SHA: `b4cbab68177c23556f0db49f8a45a431729f6e23`.
Lean `v4.32.0`; manifest mathlib SHA
`81a5d257c8e410db227a6665ed08f64fea08e997` (input `v4.32.0`).
Repository license: Apache-2.0. The large repository was searched only for
relevant group-kernel/quotient/normalizer declarations; this is not a review
of its headline mathematical claims or its entire source tree.

Inspected these nearby declarations:

- [`GroupApproximation.Full.LVHopf.ker_comp_mk'`](https://github.com/SauersML/group-approximation/blob/b4cbab68177c23556f0db49f8a45a431729f6e23/GroupApproximation/Manuscript/SimpleKazhdanSofic/Full/LVHopf/FiveTerm.lean#L35):
  for `(f : F →* G) (N : Subgroup G) [N.Normal]`,
  `((QuotientGroup.mk' N).comp f).ker = N.comap f`.
  Its proof consists of rewriting with mathlib's `MonoidHom.comap_ker` and
  `QuotientGroup.ker_mk'`. The nearby `map_ker_comp_mk'` adds surjectivity
  of `f` and concludes that this kernel's image under `f` is `N`, by
  mathlib's `Subgroup.map_comap_eq_self_of_surjective`.
- [`GroupApproximation.TypeA2.fg_of_fg_map_of_fg_inf_ker`](https://github.com/SauersML/group-approximation/blob/b4cbab68177c23556f0db49f8a45a431729f6e23/GroupApproximation/TypeA2/Extension.lean#L45):
  for `{A : Subgroup G}`,
  `(π : G →* H)`, `(hmap : (A.map π).FG)`, and
  `(hker : (A ⊓ π.ker).FG)`, it concludes `A.FG`. Its representative
  adjustment resembles the elementary step in our proof, but its result
  concerns finite generation, not an induced quotient's kernel.

Direct-use decision: reject. The kernel-composition wrapper supplies no
new prerequisite beyond pinned mathlib; the finite-generation theorem does
not imply our target. Its substantial import closure is unnecessary.
No build, axiom audit, or kernel replay was performed, so neither statement
is accepted as an externally verified proof.

## Coxeter developments and Lean 3 hits

The existing reference checkout `/tmp/artin-lean-coxeter-audit` was inspected
without modification. [`mlyean/lean-coxeter`](https://github.com/mlyean/lean-coxeter)
is at `8d36c58a038cc0642a46cf5165a1b0660348f105`, on Lean `v4.35.0`, with
mathlib manifest SHA `56a005855ea17e0b0958f73ec801ae140b0a1679`
(input `v4.35.0`), and Apache-2.0 licensing. Read its pinned version/license
files, the strong exchange statement/proof, and the geometric representation
file's initial definitions; searched the Lean sources for normalizer or
quotient-kernel results, obtaining no matches.

For example,
[`Coxeter.strong_exchange`](https://github.com/mlyean/lean-coxeter/blob/8d36c58a038cc0642a46cf5165a1b0660348f105/Coxeter/StrongExchange.lean#L51)
has ambient `{W : Type*} [CoxeterGroup W]` and, for
`{ω : List (B W)} {t : W}` and
`h : cs.IsLeftInversion (cs.wordProd ω) t`, concludes
`∃ i < ω.length, t * cs.wordProd ω = cs.wordProd (ω.eraseIdx i)`.
This is a word/inversion theorem, not a missing supplier for the arbitrary
groups/homomorphism kernel theorem. No Coxeter dependency is used by the
milestone's mathematical argument. It may warrant a separate audit for a
future article-specific Artin–Coxeter lifting/surjectivity formalization;
that problem is outside this milestone. No build, axiom audit, or kernel
replay was run for this repository here.

Search results also included mathlib3 quotient/coset sources and a project
advertising Lean 3.49.1 (`mariainesdff/norm_extensions_journal_submission`).
These are not accepted as reusable Lean 4 code; no Lean 3 theorem was silently
treated as an available Lean 4 declaration. They did not warrant a compatibility
port for already available quotient foundations.

## Search and verification record

Used public web search targeting GitHub, followed by read-only shallow Git
clones and local `rg`/source inspection. Query families included:

- `github Lean normalizer-lean F-Najman`
- `github Lean4 normalizer quotient kernel subgroup`
- `github Lean "QuotientGroup" "normalizer" -repo:leanprover-community/mathlib4`
- `site:github.com "QuotientGroup.ker_map" -leanprover-community/mathlib4 -mathlib4_docs`
- `site:github.com "normalizer" "quotient_map" lean`
- `site:github.com Lean4 group homomorphism quotient theorem normalizer`

The clones were isolated in `/tmp/lemma28-normalizer-lean`,
`/tmp/lemma28-graph-covering`, and `/tmp/lemma28-group-approximation`.
Recorded SHAs came from actual `git rev-parse HEAD`; versions and licenses
came from actual tracked files. No `lake update`, cache operation, dependency
installation, toolchain installation, or compilation was run. No shared
package state was changed.

No candidate passed the direct-use screen, so there is no proposed candidate
verification command or dependency migration for the root to execute. If a
later candidate does pass that screen, acceptance still requires a source-bound
build under agreed pinned dependencies, inspection of the elaborated complete
statement/definitions, transitive axiom checks excluding `sorryAx` and custom
axioms, and fresh kernel replay. None of these steps is asserted to have
occurred for the rejected external candidates here.

No mathematical error was established in the inspected external passages.
Unsuitability as a supplier and an unverified build are not allegations of
false mathematics. No consulted-paper defect or counterexample is asserted
by this report.

# External Lean prerequisites for the full Lemma 2.8

Research date: 2026-11-14. This search concerns the full Artin–Coxeter
normalizer-quotient surjectivity problem, beyond the completed generalized
kernel milestone. Read `CLAUDE.md` and `README.md` fully before research.
No current proof-package file was edited by this search.

## Decision and verification boundary

**TauCetiProject/TauCeti is a directly useful source candidate.** It contains
the actual Artin group given by the braid presentation, its canonical
projection to a Coxeter system, strong exchange, arbitrary standard
parabolic minimal representatives, and Matsumoto's theorem. These are proved
from definitions compatible with mathlib's Coxeter presentation, rather than
from a class assuming the desired normalizer lifting conclusion.

This report records source inspection only. It does **not** accept any
external theorem as independently verified. Compilation of the selected
closure, complete elaborated statements/definitions, transitive axiom audit
(excluding `sorryAx` and custom axioms), and fresh kernel replay are required
before reuse. Root coordinates those checks against the package's pinned
dependencies. No toolchain installation, `lake update`, cache operation,
dependency build, or shared package mutation was performed by this search.

No inspected source supplies the final normalizer-quotient surjectivity
theorem itself. Its remaining local proof must show that a minimal Coxeter
normalizer representative lifts to an Artin normalizer element, then pass to
the already formalized quotient map. Surjectivity of the ambient projection
alone does not prove surjectivity on normalizers or their quotients.

## TauCetiProject/TauCeti: preferred supplier

- Repository: <https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti>.
- Inspected SHA: `62bbc0596dc3539d488232e4e924a338548ea0a9`.
- Toolchain: `leanprover/lean4:v4.36.0-rc2`.
- Manifest mathlib SHA: `e8ba86fa9744dd8d90f48c1752bc735f61a4ca81`.
- License: Apache-2.0, confirmed in root `LICENSE` and source headers.
- Isolated source checkout: `/tmp/lemma28-full-search/tauceti`.

The current kernel package pins the same Lean version and mathlib
`65d730f7150f21fdfa32f3e73a3f549c1f96a0e9`, so compatibility must be checked;
this report does not infer it from the matching Lean version.

### Exact canonical presentation and projection

Read the full
[`Artin.lean`](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/62bbc0596dc3539d488232e4e924a338548ea0a9/TauCeti/GroupTheory/Coxeter/Artin.lean).
Its declarations are in namespace `TauCeti`:

- `artinRelation M i i'` is the free-group product of the two length
  `M i i'` braid words, with the second inverted.
- `artinRelationsSet M` is the range of all those relators.
- `ArtinGroup M` is **definitionally**
  `PresentedGroup (artinRelationsSet M)`, not a replacement group.
- `ArtinGroup.gen M i` is `PresentedGroup.of i`.
- `ArtinGroup.prod_map_gen_braidWord M i i'` proves the defining relation.
- `ArtinGroup.lift` is proved using `PresentedGroup.toGroup`.
- `ArtinGroup.toCoxeterGroup cs : ArtinGroup M →* W`, for an ordinary
  `cs : CoxeterSystem M W`, sends every Artin generator to `cs.simple i`.
- `ArtinGroup.toCoxeterGroup_surjective cs` proves ambient surjectivity from
  generation by simple reflections. It has no surjectivity premise.

The diagonal entry `M i i = 1` gives identical one-letter words and hence a
trivial relator; it does not impose the square relation. Infinite entries
are encoded by zero, for which both words are empty and the relator is also
trivial. Reversing which alternating word is listed first only inverts a
relator and does not change the braid equation. Choosing `W := M.Group` and
`cs := M.toCoxeterSystem` specializes this to mathlib's actual Coxeter
presentation. These checks rule out the relevant semantic shortcuts.

There is no Artin standard-parabolic definition in this module. Locally
defining `Subgroup.closure (ArtinGroup.gen M '' J)` gives the intended
subgroup generated by the Artin generators. Its image under the canonical
projection must be proved equal to `cs.parabolic J`, using the generator
formula and closure/map API. This is an outstanding integration obligation,
not an extra hypothesis to assume.

### Exact minimal-representative suppliers

Read the parabolic definitions, reduced-word membership lemmas, minimality
proofs and Deodhar lemma in
[`Parabolic.lean`](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/62bbc0596dc3539d488232e4e924a338548ea0a9/TauCeti/GroupTheory/Coxeter/Parabolic.lean).
These extend namespace `CoxeterSystem`, with ordinary
`{B W : Type*} [Group W] {M : CoxeterMatrix B}` and `cs : CoxeterSystem M W`:

- `cs.parabolic J := Subgroup.closure (cs.simple '' J)` (line 115).
- `exists_isReduced_wordProd_eq_of_mem_parabolic` (line 192): an element
  of `cs.parabolic J` has a reduced expression with all letters in `J`.
- `IsMinimalCosetRep J u := ∀ v ∈ cs.parabolic J,
  cs.length u ≤ cs.length (u * v)` (line 256).
- `exists_isMinimalCosetRep J w` (line 263):
  `∃ v ∈ cs.parabolic J, cs.IsMinimalCosetRep J (w * v)`.
- `length_mul_of_isMinimalCosetRep hu hv` (line 307):
  `length (u * v) = length u + length v`, for minimal `u` and
  `v ∈ cs.parabolic J`.
- `existsUnique_isMinimalCosetRep_mul J w` (line 357): unique factorization
  `w = p.1 * p.2` with minimal `p.1` and parabolic `p.2`.
- `IsMinimalCosetRep.simple_mul_or_exists_eq_mul_simple` (line 488):
  `cs.IsMinimalCosetRep J (cs.simple i * u) ∨
  ∃ j ∈ J, cs.simple i * u = u * cs.simple j`.

All these statements allow arbitrary `J : Set B`; no finite-rank or
finite-Coxeter-group hypothesis occurs. `IsMinimalCosetRep` concerns the
coset `u W_J`; multiplication-side conventions must be retained in the
local normalizer proof.

### Exact Matsumoto supplier

Read the complete
[`Matsumoto.lean`](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/62bbc0596dc3539d488232e4e924a338548ea0a9/TauCeti/GroupTheory/Coxeter/Matsumoto.lean)
and the definitions/soundness proof in `BraidEquivalence.lean`.
`CoxeterSystem.BraidEquivalent M` is `Relation.EqvGen` of the inductive
single braid replacement inside a prefix/suffix. It is not defined as
equality of evaluations.

`TauCeti.braidEquivalent_of_isReduced_wordProd_eq cs hω hω' hprod`
proves braid equivalence of reduced words with equal Coxeter product.
`TauCeti.matsumoto cs f hbraid hω hω' hprod` states

```lean
(ω.map f).prod = (ω'.map f).prod
```

for any `[Monoid G]`, `f : B → G`, and the actual braid-relation equations
`hbraid`. It requires no involution relation on `f`. Applying it to
`ArtinGroup.gen M` and `ArtinGroup.prod_map_gen_braidWord M` gives
well-defined positive reduced-word lifts in the actual Artin group.

`TauCeti.existsUnique_reducedWordLift cs f hbraid` (line 192) concludes

```lean
∃! F : W → G, ∀ ω : List B, cs.IsReduced ω →
  F (cs.wordProd ω) = (ω.map f).prod
```

This is a function, not a multiplicative homomorphism. Local integration
must prove the length-additive multiplication rule and the projection
formula; their truth must not be silently encoded as typeclass fields.
No finiteness assumption appears in these Matsumoto statements.

The proof performs induction on word length. Different initial letters are
connected through the proved rank-two descent lemma in `Dihedral.lean`;
`Geometric.Basic.lean` proves the exact order of products of simple
reflections from the concrete real geometric representation. The statements
use mathlib's ordinary presentation-based `CoxeterSystem`, not a new class
whose fields assume exchange or Matsumoto.

### Closure and source-hole screen

Following actual local imports from Artin and Matsumoto gives ten TauCeti
modules: `GroupTheory.Coxeter.{Artin,Basic,BraidEquivalence,Dihedral,
Geometric.Basic,Matsumoto,Parabolic,StrongExchange}` and
`Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Trigonometric.{Angle,Bounds}`. The generated
list is `/tmp/lemma28-full-search/tauceti/lemma28-closure.txt`.
All remaining imports in that closure are mathlib.

Source searches found no `sorry`, declaration of `axiom`, `unsafe`, or

# Landmark 1: GitHub source search for actual geometric freeness

Date: 2026-11-14. Target: the standard contragredient action of an arbitrary
finite Coxeter group, an arbitrary subset `J` of its simple indices, the real
point stabilizer theorem, and freeness of the actual `N_W(W_J)/W_J` action
on the actual relative complexified complement. Crystallographic-only
results are insufficient.

## Decision

The best directly relevant new formal supplier is still TauCeti's generic
geometric-sign development. It provides the root signs and simple-reflection
permutation of positive roots needed for a local proof of the point-stabilizer
theorem. It does not already state that theorem or complexified-complement
freeness. No directly usable general point-stabilizer/chamber theorem was
found in the additional GitHub candidates inspected.

The exact upstream Sign import closure contains nine TauCeti modules,
155,476 bytes. Seven modules are already in the unchanged parent package.
Only `Geometric/RankTwo.lean` and `Geometric/Sign.lean` are new, totaling
21,094 upstream bytes. At the parent's subsequent authorization these were
prepared under the separate `landmarks/vendor/` tree. Lake's first build
attempt with their original module paths resolved dependencies through the
parent library and failed. The parent then authorized mechanical relocation:

- `ArtinLandmarkVendor.Geometric.RankTwo` has unchanged source bytes;
- `ArtinLandmarkVendor.Geometric.Sign` substitutes its one RankTwo import
  with `ArtinLandmarkVendor.Geometric.RankTwo`;
- the original exact upstream sources remain as `.lean.txt` under
  `landmarks/vendor/upstream/`;
- mathematical declaration namespaces, statements and proofs are unchanged.

`landmarks/vendor/provenance.json` records both upstream/local hashes,
paths, the exact single import patch, all old-module references and mathlib
roots. The relocated local Lean source total is 21,086 bytes. This search
does not assert that compilation, transitive axiom audit, or kernel replay
of those sources has passed. The parent owns those acceptance checks. No
parent source, configuration, review record, vendor module, or cache was
changed by this task.

## Pinned upstream/current source

A fresh `git ls-remote ... HEAD` returned the following revisions. TauCeti
has no newer remote-HEAD chamber additions beyond the previously searched
revision.

Search queries and raw responses, exact staged candidate files, remote-HEAD

`/tmp/artin-landmark1-search/`. Temporary staging is investigative evidence,
not an installed dependency or an assertion of mathematical acceptance.

## Direct generic supplier: exact APIs and hypotheses

In
[TauCeti/GroupTheory/Coxeter/Geometric/Sign.lean](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/62bbc0596dc3539d488232e4e924a338548ea0a9/TauCeti/GroupTheory/Coxeter/Geometric/Sign.lean#L140),
the ambient parameters are just

```lean
{I W : Type*} [Group W] {M : CoxeterMatrix I} (cs : CoxeterSystem M W)
```

There is no finiteness, crystallographic, positive-definiteness, or
root-pairing hypothesis. Write `ρ = cs.geometricRepresentation` and
`α i = Finsupp.single i (1 : ℝ)`. The exact useful conclusions are:

```lean
cs.geometricRepresentation_single_pos_iff (w : W) (i : I) :
  0 < ρ w (α i) ↔ ¬ cs.IsRightDescent w i

cs.geometricRepresentation_single_neg_iff (w : W) (i : I) :
  ρ w (α i) < 0 ↔ cs.IsRightDescent w i

cs.geometricRepresentation_injective : Function.Injective ρ

cs.geometricRoots : Set (I →₀ ℝ) :=
  {v | ∃ (w : W) (i : I), ρ w (α i) = v}

cs.pos_or_neg_of_mem_geometricRoots (hv : v ∈ cs.geometricRoots) :
  0 < v ∨ v < 0

cs.ne_zero_of_mem_geometricRoots (hv : v ∈ cs.geometricRoots) : v ≠ 0

cs.geometricReflection_pos_of_mem_geometricRoots
    (hv : v ∈ cs.geometricRoots) (hpos : 0 < v) (hne : v ≠ α i) :
  0 < M.geometricReflection i v

cs.bijOn_geometricReflection_geometricRoots (i : I) :
  Set.BijOn (M.geometricReflection i)
    {v | v ∈ cs.geometricRoots ∧ 0 < v ∧ v ≠ α i}
    {v | v ∈ cs.geometricRoots ∧ 0 < v ∧ v ≠ α i}
```

The strict order on `Finsupp` means coordinatewise nonnegative and nonzero
for `0 < v`; it does not mean every coordinate is strictly positive.
The file also proves invariance of `geometricRoots` under `ρ w` and
negation. Its rank-two input is a proof via explicit trigonometric
coefficients, not an assumed root-sign property.

These declaration names remain unchanged after module relocation. The
correct new import is `ArtinLandmarkVendor.Geometric.Sign`.

The new files' direct mathlib import roots are:

```text

```

```

The full fifteen distinct mathlib roots, including private imports, are
bound in the staged `sign-closure.json` and landmark vendor provenance.
Upstream uses Lean `v4.36.0-rc2` and mathlib
`e8ba86fa9744dd8d90f48c1752bc735f61a4ca81`; the project retains mathlib
`65d730f7150f21fdfa32f3e73a3f549c1f96a0e9` and the same Lean toolchain.
Common Lean version alone does not establish compatibility.

## Closest point-stabilizer supplier: wrong hypotheses

[TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/RootSystem/FundamentalDomain.lean:188](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/62bbc0596dc3539d488232e4e924a338548ea0a9/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/RootSystem/FundamentalDomain.lean#L188)
does contain the substantive boundary stabilizer result:

```lean
TauCeti.stabilizer_eq_closure_wallReflections
    (P : RootPairing ι R M N) (b : P.Base)
    {x : M} (hx : x ∈ TauCeti.dominantChamber P b) :
  MulAction.stabilizer P.weylGroup x =
    Subgroup.closure (TauCeti.wallReflections P b x)
```

Its actual ambient hypotheses are

```lean
[CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
[AddCommGroup N] [Module R N]
[LinearOrder R] [IsStrictOrderedRing R] [Finite ι]
[P.IsCrystallographic] [P.IsReduced] [P.flip.IsReduced]
```

`wallReflections P b x` consists of simple reflections indexed by
`i ∈ b.support` with `P.coroot' i x = 0`. The proof inducts on inversion
count. This is genuinely a proved point-stabilizer statement in its model,
but it cannot be applied to the original arbitrary finite standard Coxeter
representation without new results removing/replacing the crystallographic
root-pairing assumptions and proving the model/action comparison. In
particular finite Coxeter types `H₃`, `H₄`, and general `I₂(m)` cannot be
silently discarded.

The same source family supplies
`existsUnique_mem_orbit_inter_dominantChamber_of_finite_weylGroup`, adding
`[Finite P.weylGroup]`, and `Weyl/Chamber.lean` supplies chamber freeness
and covering under the same crystallographic/reduced conditions. These are
useful proof patterns, not direct suppliers for this milestone.

The `competemath/tengoku` copy of `FundamentalDomain.lean` was fetched at its
pinned remote HEAD and its statement/hypotheses inspected. It retains
`P.IsCrystallographic`, `P.IsReduced`, and `P.flip.IsReduced`; it provides no
escape from this restriction. It is not proposed as a dependency.

## Other GitHub candidates: actual source screen

- [mlyean/lean-coxeter](https://github.com/mlyean/lean-coxeter/tree/8d36c58a038cc0642a46cf5165a1b0660348f105):
  current HEAD is unchanged from the earlier inspected exchange/Bruhat/
  geometric-representation development. No chamber/point-stabilizer
  declaration was found in its actual Coxeter sources.
- [nickgou-nuke/info-geometry-lean, CoxeterMatsumoto/Geometric.lean](https://github.com/nickgou-nuke/info-geometry-lean/blob/a392af178af1fe2bcba2ba39eb405700c6ee103c/src/InfoGeometry/Exceptional/CFSGPort/CoxeterMatsumoto/Geometric.lean):
  inspected the source, not its presentation. It constructs the standard
  representation and exact orders of products of two simple reflections.
  Its displayed endpoints are `orderOf_simple_mul_simple`, `simple_injective`,
  and related representation formulas. It contains no point-stabilizer or

- [dzackgarza/lean-categories, WeylChambers.lean](https://github.com/dzackgarza/lean-categories/blob/2b3f0449a1983ce19d05683fbc12133f5b7f4a1b/LeanCategories/Lattices/Valued/WeylChambers.lean):

## Missing bridges and a concrete generic proof route

The Sign supplier supports the following independent local route. These are
remaining obligations, not source results claimed to have been proved here:

1. Derive finite index type from `simple_injective` and finite `W`, then finite
   roots from their explicit `W × I` parametrization. Let `δ` be the sum
   of all positive geometric roots. The positive-root permutation theorem
   gives `ρ(s_i) δ = δ - 2 α_i`. Maximize `φ(ρ(w)δ)` over finite `W`;
   comparing with simple-reflection translates puts a conjugate of `φ`
   in the closed dominant chamber. This works on the actual dual standard
   representation without crystallographic assumptions.
2. Prove the dominant-point stabilizer theorem by length descent. If
   dominant `φ` is fixed by `w ≠ 1`, choose a left descent `i` of `w`.
   The Sign theorem makes `ρ(w⁻¹)α_i` negative. Its evaluation under `φ`
   equals `φ(α_i)` by invariance, while dominance makes the former
   nonpositive and the latter nonnegative. Hence `φ(α_i)=0`, so `s_i`
   fixes `φ`. Shorten `w` and induct to show that the stabilizer is
   generated by the simple reflections whose simple-root values vanish.
   Conjugate back for arbitrary real points.
3. Connect this to root-reflection generation for the actual root kernels
   and to `W_J`. A convenient route avoids proving a complete parabolic
   root-subsystem equality: define the dominant functional `c_J` with
   simple-coordinate values zero on `J` and one outside `J`. The dominant
   stabilizer theorem gives `Stab(c_J)=W_J`. A root `β` in the span of
   `J` has `c_J(β)=0`; its conjugated simple reflection fixes `c_J` by
   the geometric root-reflection formula, hence belongs to `W_J`.
   Establishing that reflection formula and the functional/span comparison
   are explicit remaining bridges. Ordinary parabolic length theory alone
   does not assert them.
4. For a pair `(φ,ψ)` in the actual relative complement, choose a real
   `t` avoiding the finitely many cancellations for root evaluations.
   Then roots vanishing on `φ+tψ` are exactly those vanishing on both
   `φ` and `ψ`; by complement membership every such root annihilates all
   of `Θ_J`, hence lies in the span of `J`. Any element fixing the pair fixes that real
   combination, so the stabilizer theorem places it in `W_J`. Combined
   with the proved trivial action of `W_J`, this gives the desired
   freeness of the quotient group, once all action/model bridges are made.
5. Invoke the actual finite-action quotient-covering construction only after
   freeness. Pinned mathlib has `Finite.to_properlyDiscontinuousSMul` and
   `isQuotientCoveringMap_quotientMk_of_properlyDiscontinuousSMul` under
   continuous constant action, Hausdorff locally compact total space and
   `IsCancelSMul`. An injective representation alone does not prove free
   action on points; a finite group alone only supplies proper discontinuity.

Used authenticated `gh search code` with Coxeter/stabilizer, geometric
representation/chamber, fixed-point, contragredient, and root-pairing
queries, followed by actual pinned raw source and local Git-object reading.
Two requests hit GitHub's search rate limit; no negative conclusion is drawn

with the full query passed as a structured field. Their responses are retained
with the other query receipts. Search result counts and names were used to
select sources to read, not as evidence that their theorems prove the target.

No external proof is accepted from this search alone. Source suitability,
compatibility compilation, transitive axiom audit, official kernel replay,
and correspondence to the actual geometric statement remain distinct checks.
No mathematical literature error was established in these readings.

# Landmark 2: positive Artin and ribbon supplier search

Research date: 2026-11-14. Scope: read-only pinned-source investigation for
the actual reduced ribbon normalizer identification in Theorem 5.6 and
the positive lcm/weak-order inputs behind (5.8) and Lemma 5.9 of
arXiv:2509.21915v3. Only this report was edited. No proof, configuration,
vendor file, review receipt, provenance or shared cache was changed.

## Decision

**Positive Artin prerequisites are present as concrete source candidates.**
The inspected openai/revised development defines the positive monoid by its
actual braid presentation, constructs its canonical map to the actual
presented Artin group, and proves spherical embedding, cancellation,
fractions, left/right gcd existence and left lcm existence. It also proves
the precise positive-lift divisibility/weak-order correspondence used in
Lemma 5.9 and identifies divisors of the fundamental element with reduced
Coxeter lifts.

**No reduced ribbon groupoid, its complete relations, or Theorem 5.6
normalizer decomposition was found.** These positive results do not by
themselves prove the requested landmark. They are candidates for filling
prerequisites, not a replacement definition of the ribbon groupoid or an
assumption of the normalizer conclusion.

Nothing is accepted as formally verified by this search. No candidate was
compiled, transitively axiom-audited, or kernel-replayed here. Source
inspection, absence of textual holes and repository claims do not replace
those acceptance steps.

## Article requirements checked

Read the full article's §5 in the workflow source `article.txt`, together
with the corresponding PDF text. In spherical type:

- Definition 5.1 has actual Artin elements as arrows, satisfying
  `A_I⁺ β = β A_K⁺`, and multiplication in `A` as rightward composition.
- Equations (5.2)–(5.4) define positive elementary ribbons from parabolic
  fundamental elements; Definition 5.5 generates the reduced subgroupoid
  using these particular arrows.
- Theorem 5.6 asserts the actual normalizer decomposition
  `Norm_A(A_J) ≅ A_J ⋊ R_J`, hence the quotient identification.
- Remark 5.7/(5.8) uses the positive left lcm and its two generating-ribbon
  expressions; the cited completeness of these relations is an additional
  theorem, not a consequence of ordinary Matsumoto.
- Lemma 5.9 uses the order isomorphism between positive reduced Coxeter
  lifts and weak left divisibility, as well as the actual ribbon/lcm
  structure, to identify these expressions with the Coxeter standard ones.

An abstract groupoid whose vertex group is defined to be the normalizer
quotient would omit these statements. No such construction is recommended.

## Pins and local source evidence

Fresh GitHub core-API HEAD checks returned the same commits already inspected:

| Repository | Commit |
| --- | --- |
| <https://github.com/openai/math> | `4eaee87548250b2682affda7d05d947c05554bae` |
| <https://github.com/mathcommunity/oai-math-revised> | `d25fae85c2f5ce5aadac40fb2b4c2d332b393d1c` |

The relevant complete `lean/OAI/Topology/ArtinGroups` tree is identical,
`0b8f7c175022e4696404bb2bbabf12746f899d14` (891 entries including
directories). Toolchain: Lean `v4.34.1`. Manifest mathlib:
`d13f23b723b8a846827a245b89c10fc7d3f11612`. Root LICENSE is Apache-2.0.
The Lake file pins other external projects, but the selected local OAI
closure below imports only OAI modules and mathlib.

The immutable source bytes came from the existing downloaded checkout under
`/tmp/lemma28-full-search/openai-math`; selected copies, closure lists and
fresh remote-check records are under `/tmp/artin-landmark2-search/`.
`openai-positive-source-inventory.json` records each selected module's path,
line count and SHA256. These temporary files are search artifacts, not build
or acceptance certificates.

## Exact positive definitions

All following names are in `OAI.HarmonicArtin`, except the `WeakPrefix`
definition in its nested `CoxeterExchange` namespace.

Read the complete
[`Coxeter/PositiveBraidRelations.lean`](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/4eaee87548250b2682affda7d05d947c05554bae/lean/OAI/Topology/ArtinGroups/Coxeter/PositiveBraidRelations.lean):

```lean
def positiveBraidRelations (u v : FreeMonoid S) : Prop :=
  ∃ s t : S, u = FreeMonoid.ofList (altList s t (M s t)) ∧
    v = FreeMonoid.ofList (altList t s (M s t))

abbrev PositiveArtin := PresentedMonoid (positiveBraidRelations M)
```

`positiveGenerator` and `wordPositive` are the canonical presented-monoid
generators and their products. `positiveToArtin : PositiveArtin M →* Artin M`
is built by `PresentedMonoid.lift`, using the actual braid equations proved
in the presented group. It maps each positive generator to `generator M s`.
Here `Artin M := PresentedGroup (braidRelators M)` from `Model.lean`.

Thus embedding is not true by a definition identifying the positive monoid
with a subset of a group. It is an actual injectivity obligation and has a
separate source proof. Zero/infinite entries give empty braid words and
diagonal entries give identical one-letter words; neither adds a square
relation to the Artin group.

`Harmonic/PositiveDegreeHom.lean` proves an additive nonnegative word degree,
with degree zero iff identity, and defines
`positiveToCoxeter : PositiveArtin M →* M.Group`.
`positiveSimpleLift M w` evaluates a chosen reduced expression in the
positive monoid, and its Coxeter image is proved to be `w`.

`Harmonic/PositivePrefix.lean` defines actual left divisibility by
`PositivePrefix M a b := ∃ c, b = a * c`; its antisymmetry follows from
degree. This is not an arbitrary ordered structure assumed to be a Garside
monoid. Right divisibility is `PositiveSuffix M a b := ∃ c, b = c * a`
in `PositiveReverseHom.lean`.

No cancellation or embedding premise in these divisor statements. |
| `Harmonic/PositivePrefix.lean` | `positivePrefix_simple_iff u v`: `PositivePrefix M (positiveSimpleLift M u) (positiveSimpleLift M v) ↔ WeakPrefix M.toCoxeterSystem u v`. | `[Fintype S]`, no finite-group or embedding premise. `WeakPrefix cs u v` is exactly `length v = length u + length (u⁻¹*v)`. Read these endpoint modules fully, together with `PositiveDegreeHom`,

definitions. Inspected the source proof of positive-word reflection and its
use of the proved probe action, rather than treating a theorem name as
evidence. I did not independently review every imported categorical/quiver

## Source closures and verification workload

Actual local import traversal, including apostrophes in module identifiers,
gave these OAI closures. All referenced OAI sources are present; the static
graphs have no import cycle. Remaining imports are mathlib.

| Endpoint module under `OAI.Topology.ArtinGroups` | OAI modules | Source lines |

| `Coxeter.PositiveBraidRelations` | 14 | 1,628 |
| `Harmonic.PositiveSimpleLiftMul` | 27 | 2,786 |

The union of the lcm and restricted-parabolic-injectivity closures has
359 modules/35,668 lines. These exact unchanged source copies and their
hash inventory are in the task's temporary candidate directory. A source
screen of that union found no `sorry`, `admit`, `sorryAx`, `native_decide`,
`implemented_by`, or custom `axiom`/`unsafe def`/`unsafe theorem`/`opaque`
declaration. This is only a screen. It does not establish successful
elaboration, compatibility with the parent mathlib pin, transitive axiom
purity, or valid kernel replay.

In particular, the large embedding proof is a different trust/porting task
from the small reduced-lift/divisor closure. No package update or build
attempt was made merely to support a suitability claim.

At root's request, the unchanged 30-module `PositivePrefix`/
`PositiveSimpleLiftMul` closure was also staged separately at
`/tmp/artin-landmark2-search/pilot-source/OAI/`. Its
`source-provenance.json` binds all source hashes, the complete dependency
graph, topological order, upstream license and pins, and the proposed
parent-toolchain target; `topological-order.txt` gives the compilation
order. This staging is not repository vendoring or a successful
compatibility result. The exact useful names are
`OAI.HarmonicArtin.positiveSimpleLift_mul`,
`OAI.HarmonicArtin.positive_fundamental_left_divisor_iff`,
`OAI.HarmonicArtin.positive_fundamental_right_divisor_iff` in
`Harmonic.PositiveSimpleLiftMul`, and
`OAI.HarmonicArtin.positivePrefix_simple_iff` in
`Harmonic.PositivePrefix`.

## Compatibility with the existing parent Artin model

The parent aliases `TauCeti.ArtinGroup M`; it must remain the actual target
group. The OAI Artin group is a second presented-group definition, **not
definitionally equal** to that alias. A canonical comparison would need
actual proofs of the following bridges:

1. Translate OAI's `altList s t n`, which starts at `s`, to mathlib/TauCeti's
   `alternatingWord s t n`, which uses its established ending convention.
   OAI proves `altList s t n = (alternatingWord t s n).reverse`;
   TauCeti proves the parity-dependent reversal identity. Hence the two
   families impose the same braid equations, possibly with their two
   sides swapped. They are not syntactically the same relator set.
2. Construct generator-preserving homomorphisms in both directions by the
   two presentation universal properties, prove both inverse laws by
   generator extensionality, and track the actual Coxeter projection.
3. Prove this isomorphism carries OAI `artinParabolic` to the existing
   parent subgroup closure. Identify the positive embedding's range with
   the submonoid generated by the actual parent Artin generators, as used
   for `A_I⁺` in Definition 5.1.
4. Transport positive reduced lifts, Delta elements, restricted-matrix
   inclusions and left/right divisibility through these actual maps.
   Positive lifts chosen by different reduced words agree by the proved
   monoid Matsumoto result; this still needs to be expressed in Lean.

The spherical embedding endpoints use a universe-zero finite ordered
ambient type and a restricted matrix on `T`. Applying `T = Set.univ` still
produces a presentation indexed by a subtype. The parent theorem permits
arbitrary indexing universes; a finite reindexing through `Fin n` and its
generator-preserving presentation equivalences must be proved if needed.
Choosing a finite order is not a new mathematical hypothesis, but it is
not a definitional transport either. No scope reduction is proposed.

The external Lean/mathlib pins also differ from the dedicated package's
mathlib `65d730f7150f21fdfa32f3e73a3f549c1f96a0e9`; no compatibility is
inferred from source inspection or from the fact that a newer Lean exists.

## What remains missing

The complete inspected ArtinGroups tree has no `ribbon` or `Garside` term,
no elementary-ribbon groupoid, and no semidirect-product normalizer
decomposition. Its normalizer hits concern unrelated parabolic-intersection
stabilizer tests. Searches for Delta also return an unrelated indicator
function in the Coxeter inversion proof; that is not a fundamental element.

Still required for the whole landmark:

- actual elementary ribbon definitions and their positive-parabolic
  conjugation identities, including sources, targets and composition;
- generation of every required monoid-preserving conjugator by ribbons
  together with its parabolic factor, with the required uniqueness;
- the actual normalizer semidirect decomposition and the induced quotient
  isomorphism, with Coxeter projection tracked;
- the two elementary-ribbon expressions of their lcm, completeness of
  the necessary ribbon relations, and their identification with the
  Coxeter standard expressions in Lemma 5.9;
- any additional groupoid composition/opposite conventions needed when
  passing to the vertex group.

The positive lcm and order correspondence are directly relevant to some
of these proofs, but none of the missing assertions is declared proved
because those prerequisites exist. In particular, a generic abstract
Garside interface assuming the normalizer decomposition would not fill
this gap.

## Search limits and source attribution

Used fresh core-API commit checks, the already complete immutable tree,
local source search and actual import traversal. No broad GitHub search
or rate-limit-dependent absence claim was used. This report covers the
openai/revised ArtinGroups development, not every file in those repositories
or every external formalization. Related sources already assessed in
`docs/full/external-prerequisites.md` were not relabeled as new suppliers.

The article's Theorem 5.6 and ribbon relations cite independent published
inputs; absence of a reusable Lean supplier is an outstanding formalization
obligation, not an open mathematical problem or a defect in the article.
No mathematical error was established in any inspected source. All
acceptance, compilation, axiom and replay limits above remain explicit.

# Landmark 2: spherical Artin and reduced-ribbon supplier search

Date: 2026-11-14. Scope: formal suppliers for the actual reduced ribbon
groupoid of `TauCeti.ArtinGroup M`, under finiteness of the actual Coxeter
group `M.Group`, with arbitrary `J` and no crystallographic restriction.
Only this document was edited; candidate sources and search receipts were
staged under `/tmp/artin-landmark2-search/other/`. No mathematical code,
configuration, vendor source, dependency pin, or shared cache was changed.

## Decision

No additional external source passed the direct-use screen for the actual
spherical-Artin reduced-ribbon/normalizer identification or its complete
presentation. The search did find an actual positive `B₃` word-normal-form
development and actual cancellation proofs for a countably generated
ordinary braid monoid. Their literal statements do not quantify over a
Coxeter matrix, do not cover all spherical types, and do not identify reduced
ribbons with the normalizer quotient. Other Garside/ribbon name matches
concern formal rewrite syntax, punctured-torus braid monoids, or specific
rank-two presentations.

Consequently no rejected external candidate was installed, compiled,
axiom-audited or kernel-replayed. None is accepted as a formally verified
supplier by this search. A README, a source comment advertising theorem
counts, an audit command in source, or an absence of textual `sorry` would
not replace the required build, transitive axiom audit and kernel replay.

## Exact target and missing strength

Read the original article's §5, Definitions 5.1 and 5.5, Theorem 5.6,
Remark 5.7 and Lemma 5.9 from `/tmp/theorem18-source.txt` (arXiv:2509.21915v3,
PDF pp. 21–23). The larger ribbon groupoid has actual Artin elements as
morphisms:

```text
Hom_R'(I,K) = { β ∈ A | A_I^+ β = β A_K^+ }.
```

Here `A_I^+` is the submonoid generated by the selected actual Artin
generators. The reduced groupoid is generated by the positive ribbons
`μ_(a,I)=Δ_I⁻¹ Δ_(I∪{a})`, with the appropriate target subset. The
required structural theorem identifies the normalizer with the semidirect
product of the actual parabolic subgroup and the actual reduced-ribbon
vertex subgroup. Its quotient consequence is the desired vertex-group
identification. A complete presentation additionally needs relations among
the ribbon generators to be complete, rather than merely true after
evaluation in the Artin group.

Defining `A^+` directly as a submonoid of the actual Artin group is legitimate
and avoids needing a separately presented monoid merely to state these
definitions. It does **not** prove cancellation/lcm/Garside normal forms or
normalizer splitting for that submonoid. Likewise an action groupoid or a
quotient built directly from the desired normalizer is not automatically
the subgroupoid generated by the article's actual ribbons.

## Pinned TauCeti and mathlib

Inspected the actual sources at TauCeti
`62bbc0596dc3539d488232e4e924a338548ea0a9` and mathlib
`65d730f7150f21fdfa32f3e73a3f549c1f96a0e9`, including the Coxeter Artin,
Matsumoto, longest-element, ordinary braid and generic normalizer-quotient
families. The relevant TauCeti tracked path inventory and focused source
searches found no Artin-monoid embedding, spherical Garside structure,
positive parabolic conjugation theorem, ribbon subgroupoid, ribbon
normalizer splitting, or complete ribbon presentation.

The available exact algebraic suppliers remain useful but weaker:

- `TauCeti.ArtinGroup M` is `PresentedGroup (artinRelationsSet M)`;
  `ArtinGroup.prod_map_gen_braidWord` proves its defining braid equality.
- `TauCeti.matsumoto cs f hbraid hω hω' hprod` identifies monoid evaluations
  of **reduced Coxeter words** with equal Coxeter product. It does not say
  arbitrary positive words equal in the Artin group are braid equivalent;
  that stronger implication would be the relevant monoid-embedding input.
- `CoxeterSystem.IsLongest w₀` in `LongestElement.lean` is defined by
  `∀ u, ℓ(u*w₀)+ℓ u=ℓ w₀`; its API proves involutivity, length reversal,
  uniqueness and parabolic-coset reversal. It concerns the Coxeter group,
  not an Artin monoid's divisibility lattice or a ribbon groupoid.
- TauCeti's `SpecificGroups/Braid/Basic.lean` defines ordinary braid groups
  as the type-`A` specialization of its actual Artin presentation. Its
  generator/braid/permutation and strand-inclusion results do not assert
  arbitrary spherical-Artin Garside or ribbon theorems.
- TauCeti's generic `Subgroup.normalizerQuotient` is exactly
  `N(H)/H`, and its lift API wraps the ordinary quotient universal property.
  It contains no spherical-Artin splitting result.

The native pinned mathlib already has the appropriate presentation
foundation:

```lean
PresentedMonoid (rels : FreeMonoid α → FreeMonoid α → Prop) :=
  (conGen rels).Quotient

PresentedMonoid.lift (f : α → N)
  (h : ∀ a b, rels a b → FreeMonoid.lift f a = FreeMonoid.lift f b) :
  PresentedMonoid rels →* N       -- [Monoid N]
```

See `Mathlib/Algebra/PresentedMonoid/Basic.lean:40,127`; `lift_of` computes
on generators, `ext` determines homomorphisms from generators, and
`mk_eq_mk_iff` identifies equality with the generated congruence.
These construct an actual Artin positive presentation and its canonical
map to the existing group, but they do not prove the map injective.

# Landmark 3: actual Coxeter chambers and wall crossings

Source inspection on 2026-11-14. Parent snapshot: `b793bf9dd4c5c9637d8dde51c6a635f849b943c4`. This inventory contains proposed new statements and inspected supplier statements; it is not a build, axiom audit, or kernel-replay acceptance record. No mathematical source, vendor, cache, or configuration was changed in this pass.

## Decision and first authoring targets

Use the existing geometric representation and actual restricted arrangement. Native proofs from pinned mathlib and the already accepted Sign provider are the shortest compatible route. The searches below found useful proof patterns, but no ready theorem identifies these restricted Coxeter chambers with atomic ribbon galleries for every finite Coxeter group.

Author these statements in this order. The names below are **proposed**, not existing APIs.

1. **Uniqueness of a dominant orbit representative**, with arbitrary `I : Type*`, no finite-group assumption:

   ```lean
   theorem dominant_action_unique (M : CoxeterMatrix I) {φ : Dual I}
       (hφ : IsDominant φ) (w : M.Group)
       (hwφ : IsDominant (dualAction M w φ)) :
       dualAction M w φ = φ
   ```

   This is a direct extension of the proof of `Landmark1.dominant_fixed_iff`. Set `ψ = dualAction M w φ`; a left descent `i` of `w` makes `ρ(w⁻¹) αᵢ` negative. Dominance of `φ` gives `ψ αᵢ ≤ 0`, dominance of `ψ` gives equality, so the simple reflection fixes `ψ`. Apply induction to `sᵢ*w`. The existing `dominant_fixed_iff` then gives `w ∈ W_(zeroIndices φ)`. This avoids the crystallographic restriction of the inspected upstream uniqueness theorem.

2. **Sign cells are the actual connected chambers**. On `E := relativeSubspace J`, define

   ```lean
   realRegularSet M J := {φ : E | Landmark1.realRelativeRegular M J φ}
   sameRootSigns M J (φ ψ : E) :=
     ∀ r ∈ retainedRoots M J, (0 < φ.val r ↔ 0 < ψ.val r)
   ```

   For regular `φ`, prove

   ```lean
   connectedComponentIn (realRegularSet M J) φ =
     {ψ | ψ ∈ realRegularSet M J ∧ sameRootSigns M J φ ψ}
   ```

   The right side is an intersection of strict linear half-spaces, hence convex. A component has constant evaluation sign by `IsPreconnected.mapsTo_Ioi_or_Iio` (or `lt_of_ne`/`gt_of_ne`). Convexity gives the reverse component inclusion. This statement does not need finiteness; openness and finite enumeration do. Use the actual subtype topology and `continuous_evaluation`, rather than importing a second normed model. Then obtain open, convex, path-connected chambers in spherical type; closure is the associated weak sign cell, by a segment from a point of the nonempty strict cell.

3. **Standard facets and their transported versions**. Define

   ```lean
   standardFacet J : Set (Dual I) :=
     {φ | (∀ i ∈ J, φ (simpleRoot i) = 0) ∧
       ∀ i ∉ J, 0 < φ (simpleRoot i)}
   ```

   Prove its canonical point is `canonicalDominant J`, its image in `relativeSubspace J` is nonempty/open/convex, and every point there is `realRelativeRegular`. For the last assertion use the Sign root dichotomy: a positive root is coordinatewise nonnegative; a retained root has a nonzero coefficient outside `J`; a strict positive evaluation there makes the finite sum strictly positive. Negative roots follow by negation. The coefficient-support/annihilator equivalence is a genuine small bridge still to author.

   For `[Finite M.Group]`, `exists_dominant_dualAction` and point-stabilizer conjugation show every actual regular point is in a transported standard facet `dualAction M w '' standardFacet K` with `w * W_K * w⁻¹ = W_J`. Prove that such a facet is a full sign cell, hence a chamber; orbit uniqueness gives uniqueness modulo its pointwise parabolic stabilizer. Do not equate the conjugacy class of subsets with all subsets of the same cardinality.

4. **The elementary geometric wall**, with `a ∉ J`, `T = insert a J`, `K = parabolicTwistImage M T J`, and `x = Artin.projection M (elementaryMu M J a)`. In the fixed flat `Θ_J`, prove that `standardFacet J` and `dualAction M x '' standardFacet K` are distinct adjacent chambers, with common wall flat `Θ_T`. A useful first local lemma is:

   ```lean
   ∀ r ∈ retainedRoots M J,
     canonicalDominant T r = 0 →
       restrictedHyperplane J r = restrictedHyperplane J (simpleRoot a)
   ```

   Indeed the root-sign dichotomy and zero evaluation at `canonicalDominant T` force its support into `T`; on `Θ_J` its evaluation is its `a` coefficient times evaluation at `αₐ`. Retention makes that coefficient nonzero. Thus this point lies on exactly one *distinct* restricted hyperplane. Prove codimension one by the coordinate model, closure incidence for both facets, and their distinction. This supplies genuine adjacency without assuming it as a ribbon axiom. Distinction needs the actual nonparabolic/minimal representative fact for `x`; it is an explicit proof obligation, not a consequence merely of Artin degree positivity.

5. **Gallery distance and geodesicity**, after the preceding geometric facts. Define separating hyperplanes as actual distinct elements of `restrictedArrangement M J` on which two chamber signs differ. Prove adjacency changes exactly one such sign, gallery length is bounded below by their number, and a suitable generic segment gives a gallery crossing each separator once. Then establish the relative inversion/separation formula for transported facets, so the existing length-additive pair-lcm atomic words become actual geodesic galleries. `AtomicCoxeter` alone does not supply this conclusion. In particular, do not identify one atomic edge with Coxeter length one: its weight is `ℓ(π μ)`, which can be larger than one.

All five stages retain arbitrary index universes. Obtain `Finite I` from `Geometry.finite_index M`, then use `Fintype.ofFinite` locally where finite intersections/sums are needed. Avoid `I : Type` restrictions and unnecessary reindexing of geometry. For `J = univ`, `Θ_J = 0`, there are no retained hyperplanes and exactly one chamber; there are no outside atomic labels. For `J = ∅` these definitions recover the ordinary dual chamber arrangement. The rank-zero case is included.

## Existing actual models and accepted local inputs

Inspected the complete relevant parent files, not just their descriptions:

* `ArtinNormalisers/Theorem18/Geometry.lean`: `Vector I := I →₀ ℝ`; `Dual I := Module.Dual ℝ (Vector I)`; topology induced by `dualCoordinatesHomeomorph : Dual I ≃ₜ (I → ℝ)`. `relativeSubspace J` is the submodule annihilating the selected simple roots. `root M w i := M.toCoxeterSystem.geometricRepresentation w (simpleRoot i)`. `roots M` consists of these actual orbit roots; `retainedRoots M J` additionally requires a nonzero restriction to the flat. `restrictedHyperplane J r` is the kernel of that restriction and `restrictedArrangement M J` its image over retained roots, so repeated/proportional roots give one actual hyperplane. `Complement M J` is the subtype of pairs of real flat points on no `H × H`. `finite_index`, `roots_finite`, `retainedRoots_finite`, and openness of the actual complement are already proved under `[Finite M.Group]`.
* `ArtinNormalisers/Theorem18/NormalizerAction.lean`: `dualAction M : Representation ℝ M.Group (Dual I)` satisfies `dualAction M w φ v = φ (ρ(w⁻¹) v)`. `mem_relativeSubspace_iff_fixed` identifies the flat with the pointwise fixed space of the actual generated parabolic. The actual normalizer quotient acts through `quotientRepresentation` on the flat and `quotientComplementAction` on the complement; continuity is proved in the coordinate topology. `OrbitSpace` is the actual orbit-relation quotient with quotient topology.
* `landmarks/ArtinLandmarks/Dominant.lean`: `IsDominant φ := ∀ i, 0 ≤ φ (simpleRoot i)`; `zeroIndices φ := {i | φ (simpleRoot i) = 0}`. Literal key conclusion:

  ```lean
  dominant_fixed_iff (hφ : IsDominant φ) (w : M.Group) :
    dualAction M w φ = φ ↔
      w ∈ Artin.coxeterParabolic M (zeroIndices φ)
  ```

  Also `canonicalDominant_fixed_iff` and `pointwise_flat_fixed_iff` for every `J`, with no finite-group assumption.
* `landmarks/ArtinLandmarks/RegularStabilizer.lean`: under `[Finite M.Group]`,

  ```lean
  exists_dominant_dualAction (φ : Dual I) :
    ∃ u, IsDominant (dualAction M u φ)
  realRelativeRegular M J (φ : relativeSubspace J) : Prop :=
    ∀ r ∈ retainedRoots M J, φ.val r ≠ 0
  realRelativeRegular_fixed_iff φ hφ g :
    dualAction M g φ.val = φ.val ↔ g ∈ Artin.coxeterParabolic M J
  ```

* `landmarks/ArtinLandmarks/Covering.lean` proves actual complement-pair stabilizers, free quotient action, actual orbit covering, and its fundamental-group short exact sequence. It defines no real chamber, facet, crossing, or gallery.
* `ribbons/ArtinRibbons/AtomicCoxeter.lean`: `projection_positiveToParent`, `projection_parentSimpleLift`, `degree_eq_coxeterLength_of_simple`, `elementaryMu_degree_eq_coxeterLength`, and

  ```lean
  AtomicWord.coxeter_length_additive_of_simple (p : AtomicWord M X Y)
      (h : ∃ w, p.eval = positiveToParent M (positiveSimpleLift M w)) :
    M.toCoxeterSystem.length (Artin.projection M p.eval) = p.coxeterWeight
  AtomicWord.pairLcm_coxeter_length_additive p a b
      (he : p.eval = pairRibbonLcm M X.indices a b) :
    M.toCoxeterSystem.length (Artin.projection M p.eval) = p.coxeterWeight
  ```

  Here `coxeterWeight` is the sum of the Coxeter lengths of the traversed elementary projections. `AtomicWord.length` counts atomic edges and is a different quantity. `RibbonLcm.pairRibbonLcm_weakPrefix_join` already proves the algebraic weak-prefix join for the two longest-element ratios; no upstream weak-order geometry needs to be invented as a hypothesis.

**Action convention.** An actual ribbon `r : J → K` conjugates `W_J` to `W_K` by `x⁻¹ W_J x`, for `x = π(r)`. Consequently the target chamber drawn in the *source* flat is `x · C_K ⊆ Θ_J`. Appending `s : K → L` gives `x y · C_L`, agreeing with `AtomicWord.eval` putting the first traversed label on the left. Neither this convention nor geometric equivariance should be silently inverted.

## Pinned supplier inspection

Mathlib pin: `65d730f7150f21fdfa32f3e73a3f549c1f96a0e9`, inspected at `/tmp/artin-mathlib-audit`. TauCeti accepted pin: `62bbc0596dc3539d488232e4e924a338548ea0a9`, inspected at `/tmp/lemma28-full-search/tauceti`. The accepted geometric Sign closure is already available locally under the relocated `ArtinLandmarkVendor.Geometric.Sign` import; it must not be duplicated or replaced for this task.

### Directly useful mathlib APIs

`Mathlib/Topology/Connected/Basic.lean` contains the following literal generic statements (usual topology variables suppressed):

```lean
IsPreconnected.mapsTo_Ioi_or_Iio (hs : IsPreconnected s)
    (hf : ContinuousOn f s) (hfb : ∀ x ∈ s, f x ≠ b) :
  Set.MapsTo f s (Set.Ioi b) ∨ Set.MapsTo f s (Set.Iio b)
IsPreconnected.lt_of_ne (hs : IsPreconnected s) (hf : ContinuousOn f s)
    (hfb : ∀ x ∈ s, f x ≠ b) (hfx : ∃ x ∈ s, b < f x)
    (hx : x ∈ s) : b < f x
IsPreconnected.subset_connectedComponentIn (hs : IsPreconnected s)
    (hxs : x ∈ s) (hsF : s ⊆ F) : s ⊆ connectedComponentIn F x

Also `connectedComponentIn_subset`, `isPreconnected_connectedComponentIn`, `ContinuousOn.image_connectedComponentIn_subset`. `Mathlib/Analysis/Convex/Basic.lean` has `convex_iInter`, `convex_halfSpace_lt`, `convex_halfSpace_gt` and affine/linear preimages of convex intervals. `Mathlib/Analysis/Convex/PathConnected.lean` has

```

These work on real topological vector spaces; no norm or integral lattice is needed for the native chamber proofs. `Mathlib/GroupTheory/Coxeter/Inversion.lean` supplies `IsReflection`, left/right inversions, inversion sequences and nodup of both sequences for a reduced word; it does not identify these with actual separating geometric hyperplanes. `Length.lean` supplies reduced expressions, prefix/tail reducedness, descent criteria, `length_inv`, and multiplication bounds. These are algebraic inputs only.

### TauCeti Sign: compatible and already accepted

`TauCeti/GroupTheory/Coxeter/Geometric/Sign.lean`, namespace `CoxeterSystem`, arbitrary `I : Type*`, group `W`, `cs : CoxeterSystem M W`:

```lean
geometricRepresentation_single_pos_iff (w : W) (i : I) :
  0 < cs.geometricRepresentation w (Finsupp.single i 1) ↔ ¬cs.IsRightDescent w i
geometricRepresentation_single_neg_iff (w : W) (i : I) :
  cs.geometricRepresentation w (Finsupp.single i 1) < 0 ↔ cs.IsRightDescent w i
pos_or_neg_of_mem_geometricRoots (hv : v ∈ cs.geometricRoots) : 0 < v ∨ v < 0

Root invariance, negation invariance, norm one, simple-reflection preservation of other positive roots, and faithful representation are also proved. This is the correct noncrystallographic supplier.

`Geometric/Transport.lean` gives `mapDomain_geometricRepresentation`, `geometricRepresentation_reindex`, and `geometricRepresentation_reindexGroupEquiv_symm`; those are optional transport APIs if a finite-index equivalence is needed. They do not construct chamber geometry.

### TauCeti RootPairing chambers: conclusions inspected, extra hypotheses incompatible

`LinearAlgebra/RootSystem/Chamber.lean` defines `RootPairing.IsRegularWeight P x := ∀ i, P.coroot' i x ≠ 0`, `dominantChamber P b := {x | ∀ i ∈ b.support, 0 ≤ P.coroot' i x}`, and its strict version. `exists_mem_dominantChamber_of_finite_weylGroup` concludes `∃ w : P.weylGroup, w • x ∈ dominantChamber P b`, but its section assumes `[Finite ι] [P.IsCrystallographic] [P.IsReduced]` in addition to ordered-ring/module conditions and finite Weyl group.

`LinearAlgebra/RootSystem/FundamentalDomain.lean` proves

```lean

## TauCeti: actual open-cover groupoid gluing

All paths in this section are relative to `TauCeti/`, and names are in
`TauCeti.FundamentalGroupoid` unless explicitly qualified.

### Literal spaces, diagram, and colimit

[`Topology/Category/TopCat/Cech/Diagram.lean`](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/62bbc0596dc3539d488232e4e924a338548ea0a9/TauCeti/Topology/Category/TopCat/Cech/Diagram.lean)
defines, for `X : TopCat` and `U : ι → Opens X`,

```lean
abbrev CechIndex (ι : Type u) := OrderDual {s : Finset ι // s.Nonempty}
def cechIntersection (s : CechIndex ι) : Opens X := s.1.inf U
```

Here nonempty means the **index finite set**, not an assumption that the
intersection itself contains a point. Empty and disconnected intersections
are allowed. The topological diagram consists of the actual subtype spaces
`TopCat.of (cechIntersection U s)` and actual inclusions, ordered by reverse
inclusion of finite index sets.

[`AlgebraicTopology/FundamentalGroupoid/Cech/Diagram.lean`](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/62bbc0596dc3539d488232e4e924a338548ea0a9/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/FundamentalGroupoid/Cech/Diagram.lean)
defines

```lean
def cechDiagram : CechIndex ι ⥤ Grpd :=
  cechTopDiagram U ⋙ _root_.FundamentalGroupoid.fundamentalGroupoidFunctor
```

`cechCocone U` is the image under that same Mathlib functor of the cocone
of inclusions into `X`. Its point is definitionally the actual fundamental
groupoid of `X`, not a freely generated substitute.

The main endpoint in
[`Cech/Colimit.lean`, line 125](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/62bbc0596dc3539d488232e4e924a338548ea0a9/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/FundamentalGroupoid/Cech/Colimit.lean#L125)
is exactly

```lean
def isColimitCechCocone (hU : IsOpenCover U) : IsColimit (cechCocone U)
```

There is no connectedness, contractibility, good-cover, finiteness, or
arrangement hypothesis. The only additional hypothesis is that `U` covers.
The result is a strict categorical colimit in `Grpd`; it is not a theorem
that the geometric realization of a nerve is homotopy equivalent to `X`.
That distinction prevents upgrading it to an asphericity theorem.

### The comparison functor is constructed from genuine paths

[`Glue.lean`](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/62bbc0596dc3539d488232e4e924a338548ea0a9/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/FundamentalGroupoid/Glue.lean)
works more generally with `U : ι → Set X` and

```lean
hU : ∀ x, ∃ i, U i ∈ 𝓝 x
F : ∀ i, _root_.FundamentalGroupoid (U i) ⥤ D
hF : ∀ i j,
  map (ContinuousMap.inclusion inter_subset_left) ⋙ F i =
  map (ContinuousMap.inclusion inter_subset_right) ⋙ F j
```

for any target category `D`. It constructs
`glue hU F hF : _root_.FundamentalGroupoid X ⥤ D`.
The proof subdivides paths using a Lebesgue number, evaluates each segment
in a cover piece, proves independence of subdivision, and subdivides an
actual path homotopy into small squares to prove homotopy invariance.
`map_subtypeVal_comp_glue` proves the required local restriction equation;
`eq_glue` proves uniqueness. The local agreement `hF` is the legitimate
input for gluing, not an assumed global equivalence to the target.

`CoverGeneration.iSup_im_map_subtypeVal_eq_top` proves that actual cover
inclusion functors generate the fundamental groupoid; `functor_ext` makes
local equality sufficient for global equality. These may be useful even
if the final construction uses explicit functors instead of colimits.

### Actual continuous-map naturality and equivariance limit

[`Cech/Map.lean`](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/62bbc0596dc3539d488232e4e924a338548ea0a9/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/FundamentalGroupoid/Cech/Map.lean)

```lean

  hU.desc (cechMapCocone U V f r hf) =

```

Thus the source colimit hypothesis can be discharged by the preceding
open-cover theorem. No target cover hypothesis is needed for this equality.

action on cover indices would instantiate this theorem. It does not
construct that action, prove that it preserves a chosen arrangement cover,

# Landmark 3: other GitHub source search

Date: 2026-11-14. This report concerns the actual complement defined in
`ArtinNormalisers/Theorem18/Geometry.lean`, not a substitute classifying space.
The complete geometry file, repository README and landmark plan were read first.
Landmarks 1 and 2 remain proved; this search adds no proof of landmark 3.

## Result and actionable candidate

No inspected repository outside the separately assigned TauCeti/OpenAI search
supplies the full equivariant restricted-arrangement comparison. The closest
actionable generic supplier is **qinz1yang/differential-geometry's genuine
two-open fundamental-groupoid Seifert–van Kampen theorem**, with an eight-file
project import closure. Its literal theorem uses actual topological spaces
and proves a pushout; it does not assume the pushout as a structure field.
It is an alternate generic supplier, not an accepted imported proof.

The other especially relevant search result, the Chen-ranks development,
does define an actual finite complex affine arrangement complement and true
polygonal-path homotopies. It supplies neither the chamber presentation nor
the required comparison/equivariance in the inspected source. Its basic
convex-ball cover is not itself a nerve comparison.

**Execution status for every candidate in this report:** source inspected
only; no build, transitive axiom audit or kernel replay was run. No proof,
configuration or vendor file was modified; no new proof source was copied
or imported. No `lake update`, cache operation or toolchain installation was
performed. A lexical no-hole scan is explicitly not formal verification.

## Exact target boundary

The parent's `Complement M J` is the subtype of
`relativeSubspace J × relativeSubspace J` consisting of pairs `(x,y)` such
that, for every retained actual root `r`, the evaluations `x r` and `y r`
are not both zero. It has the inherited product/subspace topology, transported
from the actual dual coordinates. Retained roots discard those identically
zero on the relative flat; equal restricted hyperplanes are identified in
`restrictedArrangement M J`.

The desired supplier must connect this actual complement to a groupoid
whose generators are geometric positive crossings and whose relations have
been proved to hold and be complete. Reverse positive crossings are separate
generators, not formal inverses. A homotopy-equivalence transport theorem
alone does not construct that equivalence. A generic open-cover theorem
alone does not identify its colimit with the ribbon/Deligne presentation.
The eventual comparison must track the actual normalizer-quotient action and
the `J`-associate component; it cannot assume the quotient acts transitively
on all chambers or use all subsets as one relevant component without proof.
