## Literal strongest generic theorem

At the pinned qinz1yang commit,
[`DifferentialGeometry/Topology/VanKampen/FullGroupoid.lean`](https://github.com/qinz1yang/differential-geometry/blob/13c41a632efb8fbf93101c8a20f2a9214ab33240/DifferentialGeometry/Topology/VanKampen/FullGroupoid.lean)
defines `fullGroupoidSquareIsPushoutStatement U V` as the actual `IsPushout`
in `Grpd` of these four objects and continuous inclusion-induced functors:

```text
FundamentalGroupoid (U ∩ V) → FundamentalGroupoid U
             ↓                         ↓
FundamentalGroupoid V       → FundamentalGroupoid X.
```

The exact exported declaration is:

```lean
theorem seifertVanKampen {X : Type u} [TopologicalSpace X] (U V : Set X)
    (hU : IsOpen U) (hV : IsOpen V) (hcover : U ∪ V = univ) :
    fullGroupoidSquareIsPushoutStatement U V
```

The namespace is `DifferentialGeometry.Topology.VanKampen`. No path-connectedness,
simply-connectedness, local-contractibility or dimension assumption is hidden
in this declaration. In `Evaluation.lean`, `LocalFunctorData U V G` contains
only functors from the two actual fundamental groupoids into `G`, plus their
agreement after restriction to `U ∩ V`. Its `extension` is **constructed** by
path subdivision and evaluation, descended through proved homotopy invariance;
its extension and uniqueness properties produce the pushout proof. No
extension-existence or desired pushout field is assumed in that data.

Its project closure is exactly these eight modules, in a possible dependency
build order:

1. `DifferentialGeometry.Topology.VanKampen.Subdivision`
2. `DifferentialGeometry.Topology.VanKampen.CoveredPath`
3. `DifferentialGeometry.Topology.VanKampen.Evaluation`
4. `DifferentialGeometry.Topology.VanKampen.HomotopyGrid`
5. `DifferentialGeometry.Topology.VanKampen.CellIdentity`
6. `DifferentialGeometry.Topology.VanKampen.GroupoidTelescope`
7. `DifferentialGeometry.Topology.VanKampen.HomotopyInvariance`
8. `DifferentialGeometry.Topology.VanKampen.FullGroupoid`

All remaining imports are mathlib modules: fundamental groupoid basics,
composable arrows, groupoids, categorical pushouts, product homotopies,
metric-space lemmas and subpaths. A lexical scan with comments removed found
no `sorry`, `admit`, `axiom`, `native_decide` or `unsafe` token in this closure.
That scan neither checks elaboration nor certifies transitive axioms.

Possible actual application: choose genuine open subsets of `Complement M J`,
prove they cover, and apply the theorem to construct/characterize its
fundamental groupoid from the restrictions. For a finite chamber-indexed
cover, one would still have to derive the iterated/multiple-overlap colimit,
identify all intersection components and their paths/relations, and prove the
Deligne/ribbon presentation and normalizer equivariance. These are substantial
new bridges, not consequences of this theorem's name. The separately examined
TauCeti Čech theorem may be a more direct generic API; do not import two
parallel van Kampen implementations without need.

If selected after the actual-cover route is fixed, verification should copy
only this unchanged eight-module closure into an isolated test package using
the project's existing Lean/mathlib pins, preserving Apache headers and
binding upstream/local hashes. A proposed initial command, **not run here**,
is `lake build DifferentialGeometry.Topology.VanKampen.FullGroupoid` after
declaring that test library. Then inspect its elaborated statement and audit
all declarations of all eight modules, allowing only `propext`,
`Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`; run the existing project's supported
single-module checker form for each module. The upstream package's older
toolchain is not a reason to replace this project's pins. A successful
upstream build alone would not certify the port or its application.

## Literal definitions behind the other close results

The Chen-ranks repository's `ChenRanks.AffineArrangement d ι` has a finite
index type and fields `normal : ι → (Fin d → ℂ) →ₗ[ℂ] ℂ`, `offset : ι → ℂ`,
nonzero normals, and pairwise distinct equation zero sets. It defines

```lean
def Complement := {x : Fin d → ℂ // ∀ i, A.normal i x ≠ A.offset i}
```

with the induced topology. Its `actualPolygonalApproximationHomotopy`, for an
actual `γ : Path x y` in `A.Complement`, constructs a fixed-endpoint path
homotopy from the actual polygonal approximation to the full subpath of `γ`.
`ActualComplementBall` contains an actual center/radius, positivity and proof
the ambient ball lies in the complement; `actualComplementBallAt` constructs
such a ball at each point from proved openness, and
`mem_actualComplementBallBaseSet_at` proves the resulting cover property.

This is not a surrogate space. To apply it here requires a proved finite
complex-coordinate identification of the relative real-pair vector space,
complexification of the distinct retained hyperplanes, and equality of the
two removed sets/topologies. Such a bridge is mathematically possible but was
not constructed by this search. These results still do not supply homotopy
**completeness** of chamber relations or equivariance. Existing project
path-connectedness already addresses a simpler part of this geometry.

The jacobian repository's `TwoOpenVanKampen` expands to: every path-connected
topological `Z : Type` covered by open simply-connected `U,V` with
path-connected intersection is simply connected. Its
`Jacobians.RiemannSphere.VanKampen.twoOpenVanKampen_holds` proves that exact
proposition by actual subdivisions, spokes and path-homotopy telescoping.
It is a genuine corollary, but cannot replace a presentation of the generally
nontrivial fundamental groupoid of a hyperplane complement.

The pytop file is a concrete rejected assumed-conclusion case:
`VanKampen.Pushout datum A` contains only `i₁`, `i₂`, and their compatibility
for **additive commutative** groups. `pushout_universal` is given an arbitrary
`u : A →+ K` plus
`hu₁ : ∀ g₁, u (po.i₁ g₁) = f₁ g₁` and
`hu₂ : ∀ g₂, u (po.i₂ g₂) = f₂ g₂`; its conclusion is just the conjunction
of those equations for each pair `(g₁,g₂)`. Its proof is
`fun g₁ g₂ => ⟨hu₁ g₁, hu₂ g₂⟩`. It constructs no universal factor or
topological path identification. The file's own Scope paragraph states this
limitation; no false topological theorem is attributed to it.

Polylean's `FundamentalGroupoid` is an instance on a
`CombinatorialTwoComplex`: its homs are quotients of combinatorial edge paths
by an inductively defined relator homotopy. It uses a custom `Groupoid` and
`SerreGraph` reversal. It does not prove those are topological paths of a
realized space, so naming it a fundamental groupoid does not fill the bridge.

The two Kang repositories' exact useful form is
`SSet.realizationSimplicialHomotopy (H : SSet.Homotopy f g) :
(SSet.toTop.map f).hom.Homotopy (SSet.toTop.map g).hom`, and the analogous
homotopy of classifying maps from a natural transformation `α : F ⟶ G`.
These relate actual realizations, but no map from our complement, chamber
good cover, or equivariant homotopy inverse is present in the inspected file.

## Existing mathlib APIs and duplication screen

At the project's existing pin,
`FundamentalGroupoidFunctor.equivOfHomotopyEquiv (e : X ≃ₕ Y)` already gives
an equivalence of the actual fundamental groupoids. The neighboring
`homotopicMapsNatIso` constructs the natural transformation of path-class
functors from an actual continuous homotopy. The sphere-six-complex wrapper
then takes endomorphism groups via fully faithfulness; this supplies no new
geometric comparison.

`Convex.contractibleSpace (hs : Convex ℝ s) (hne : s.Nonempty)` already proves
`ContractibleSpace s` in a real topological vector space with continuous
addition and scalar multiplication. This is suitable for genuine convex
finite intersections of a proposed good cover once their inclusion/cover
conditions have been proved. The existing dual-coordinate topology supplies
the appropriate continuous vector-space structure. None of these facts
identifies a nerve with the actual complement by itself.

Searched the pinned fundamental-groupoid/simplicial-groupoid modules and
related file names for a ready-made open-cover comparison. No such result
was located in that bounded inspection; this is not an assertion about all
future or uninspected mathlib declarations.

## Search record, provenance and limits

Used `gh search repos`, `gh search code`, raw pinned GitHub URLs via Python's
HTTPS client, and isolated `/tmp` shallow clones. Search terms included
`Salvetti`, `DeligneGroupoid`, `HyperplaneArrangement`, `FundamentalGroupoid`,
`vanKampen`, `hyperplane complement`, `complexified`, `GoodCover`, and
`nerve contractible`, with Lean/`.lean` filters and a second pass explicitly
excluding `openai/math` and `leanprover-community/mathlib4`.

The observed `Salvetti`, `DeligneGroupoid`, and explicit excluded-repository
`Deligne groupoid`, `complexified`, `GoodCover`, `nerve contractible` queries
returned no results. This is a GitHub-index/API observation, not proof of
worldwide absence. Several earlier requests received HTTP 429/403 search-rate
errors; the affected later query families were retried successfully in the
second pass. Search is bounded by indexing, branch selection and result caps.

The temporary machine inventory is `/tmp/m3-other-inventory.json`. It has
the twelve source-inspected repositories, full commits, licenses, source
hashes, declaration names, application/disposition, reading limits and
explicit false build/audit/replay/acceptance flags. It separately lists
twenty-eight repositories appearing as code-search hits, without calling
those hits proof use. Query records are in
`/tmp/milestone3-other-search.json` and `/tmp/m3-search-round2.json`;
the full qinz import/hash inventory is
`/tmp/m3-qinz-fullgroupoid-closure.json`. These temporary inventories are
provided for the root's central provenance register; this report is the only
repository file authored by this task.

# Landmark 4: exact vertex-group and basepoint prerequisites

Research date: 2026-11-14. Baseline repository:
`1aa55a9ee5f13c9e3a8e64b4aec4675c0435a9c0`. Read the complete
[`milestone4-PLAN.md`](milestone4-PLAN.md), the current main landmark plan,
and the actual M1/M2/M3 map APIs before proposing reuse. No earlier scientific,
configuration or review source was changed by this search.

## Selected result and present verification status

Root selected **exactly two TauCeti declarations**, extracted verbatim into
`ArtinSequenceVendor.FundamentalGroup.BasepointChange`, from
`TauCetiProject/TauCeti` at `62bbc0596dc3539d488232e4e924a338548ea0a9`:

- `FundamentalGroup.fundamentalGroupMulEquivOfPath_apply`, original lines
  129–148 including its documentation and local namespace opening.
- `FundamentalGroup.map_fundamentalGroupMulEquivOfPath`, original lines
  196–212 including its documentation and local namespace opening.

The complete original 651-line file, Apache-2.0 license, original copyright
header, selected-block hashes, full mechanical diff and deterministic assembly
recipe are preserved in [`sequences/vendor/`](../../../sequences/vendor/README.md).
The original namespace and both declaration/proof blocks remain unchanged;
the new wrapper imports only two existing pinned mathlib modules. The full
upstream BasepointChange file and its unrelated dependencies are not imported.

The actual selected module passed explicit Lake compilation, exhaustive
canonical/physical transitive axiom audit and fresh exact-module official
`leanchecker` replay. Coverage measured **2 canonical declarations, 2 physical
occurrences, no duplicates**, with only `propext`, `Classical.choice` and
`Quot.sound`. The measured replay took 5.87 seconds. Inputs were unchanged
through audit and replay. Raw commands/logs/hashes, displayed elaborated
statements and environment bindings are in
[`sequences/evidence/providers/verification.json`](../../../sequences/evidence/providers/verification.json).
Replay is relative to imported pinned mathlib, not a new replay of all mathlib
or an independent kernel implementation.

**The technical record predates independent acceptance.** Both independent
supplier review receipts are now available in `sequences/reviews/providers-a.json`
and `providers-b.json`, with verdict `accept-supplier-cohort`; their hashes are
recorded in the inventory. Root mathematical acceptance is not asserted here.
Technical success is not reported as completion of landmark 4. The generic alternatives below remain
source-inspected candidates; they were not compiled, audited or replayed by
this search. No new FormalFrontier, Oka, sphere-six or other source was imported.

## Directly usable existing APIs

The project uses Lean `v4.36.0-rc2` and mathlib
`65d730f7150f21fdfa32f3e73a3f549c1f96a0e9`. These are the actual inspected
local sources, not assumptions based on current online documentation.

| Need | Exact API and type/application |
| --- | --- |
| Take vertex groups of the M3 equivalences | `CategoryTheory.Functor.FullyFaithful.mulEquivEnd (hf : FullyFaithful F) (X : C) : End X ≃* End (F.obj X)`, in `Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Endomorphism.lean:217`. Apply an M3 equivalence's `.fullyFaithfulFunctor`. This uses the actual functor, preserving its map on arrows. |
| Induced homomorphism on vertex groups | `CategoryTheory.Functor.mapEnd` in the same file: `End X →* End (F.obj X)`. Restrict the already proved strict M3 functor square, using its object equality and `eqToIso` where necessary. |
| Actual fundamental-group model | `FundamentalGroup X x` is literally `End (FundamentalGroupoid.mk x)`. `FundamentalGroup.mul_def` is `.of (q.asHom.trans p.asHom)` for `p * q`: categorical/loop multiplication order must be tracked. Source: `Mathlib/AlgebraicTopology/FundamentalGroupoid/FundamentalGroup.lean`. |
| Continuous-map homomorphism | `FundamentalGroup.map (f : C(X,Y)) (x : X)` maps to the group at `f x`. `mapOfEq f (h : f x = y)` maps to the group at the specified `y`. `mapOfEq_apply` gives the path-class map followed by endpoint casts using `h.symm` twice. |
| Actual basepoint transport | `FundamentalGroup.fundamentalGroupMulEquivOfPath (θ : Path x₀ x₁) : FundamentalGroup X x₀ ≃* FundamentalGroup X x₁`. It is `Iso.conj` of the actual path class, not a separately chosen abstract group equivalence. |
| Map/basepoint naturality foundation | `CategoryTheory.Functor.map_conj` in `Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Conj.lean` maps `α.conj f` to `(F.mapIso α).conj (F.mapEnd X f)`, on underlying arrows. This is the exact existing supplier used by the selected TauCeti naturality proof. |
| Evaluate actual endpoint monodromy | `IsQuotientCoveringMap.fundamentalGroupToMulOpposite_apply_mk_eq`, in `Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/Lifting.lean:664`, takes a loop `γ`, a continuous lift `Γ`, `p ∘ Γ = γ`, `Γ 0 = e`, and `Γ 1 = g • e`, and concludes the raw monodromy is `MulOpposite.op g`. |
| Evaluate using a path class rather than a representative | `fundamentalGroupToMulOpposite_apply_eq_iff` states that raw label `g : Gᵐᵒᵖ` is equivalent to `g.unop • e = monodromy γ.asHom e`. `IsCoveringMap.monodromy_eq_of_map_eq`, `monodromy_map`, `map_liftPathQuotient`, and `monodromy_trans_apply` supply the lift/class and concatenation calculations. |
| Move the selected lift within a fiber | `IsQuotientCoveringMap.fundamentalGroupToMulOpposite_toPermFiber` gives raw label `op (g * oldLabel.unop * g⁻¹)` after moving the lift by `g`. This is a conjugation law, not basepoint independence for a noncommutative quotient. |
| Normalize the opposite convention honestly | `MulEquiv.inv' G : G ≃* Gᵐᵒᵖ` in `Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Equiv/Opposite.lean:71`. Its inverse sends `op g` to `g⁻¹`. Plain `op`/`unop`, or inversion within a noncommutative group, is not silently used as a homomorphism. |

The literal selected statements, with arbitrary topological spaces and no
connectivity/covering hypotheses, are:

```lean
FundamentalGroup.fundamentalGroupMulEquivOfPath γ g =
  .of ((Path.Homotopic.Quotient.mk γ).symm.trans
    (g.asHom.trans (Path.Homotopic.Quotient.mk γ)))

FundamentalGroup.map f x₁ (FundamentalGroup.fundamentalGroupMulEquivOfPath γ g) =
  FundamentalGroup.fundamentalGroupMulEquivOfPath (γ.map f.continuous)
    (FundamentalGroup.map f x₀ g)
```

The second formula is exactly the covering-induced-map/basepoint square.
For landmark 4 choose one actual upstairs path `θ` and **its image under the
actual orbit projection** downstairs. The first formula, mathlib's monodromy
concatenation law and `monodromy_toPermFiber` compute raw endpoint monodromy
under that paired transport. Independent downstairs path choices would
introduce conjugation, so path-connectedness alone does not prove the desired
identity on the same Coxeter quotient.

## Existing actual M1/M2/M3 suppliers and application limits

- `ArtinNormalisers.Landmark1.orbitFundamentalGroupMap`, `orbitMonodromy` and
  `orbitFundamentalGroup_shortExact`, in `landmarks/ArtinLandmarks/Covering.lean`,
  are the actual orbit-map homomorphism, raw monodromy into the **opposite**
  actual Coxeter normalizer quotient, and their short exactness at every
  actual complement basepoint.
- `Ribbon2.reducedRibbonNormalizerQuotientEquiv` in
  `ribbons/ArtinRibbons/NormalizerSplitting.lean` is the actual canonical
  reduced-loop-label quotient map proved bijective in M2. The larger ribbon
  group's `endEquivRibbonLoopsOpposite` in `RibbonGroupoid.lean` is useful for
  recognizing the convention, but is not the reduced associate-component
  vertex identification needed by M4.
- `Chamber3.actualIntervalComplementEquivalence`,
  `actualRibbonOrbitEquivalence` and `actualComparison_square` are actual M3
  equivalences and the strictly commuting covering square. Taking `End` and
  transporting the literal object equalities yields the middle comparison;
  it does not by itself identify the canonical Coxeter label.
- `chambers/ArtinChambers/RibbonDeckLabels.lean` supplies the already proved
  signed endpoint projection. Combine that formula with the actual M3 lifted
  path class and mathlib's endpoint evaluation before normalizing `Qᵐᵒᵖ→Q`.
  This avoids treating two unrelated isomorphisms as a commuting diagram.

These earlier accepted sources were read as prerequisite context, not modified
or re-certified. The new M4 `BasepointTransport.lean` source actually references

lifts `g e = e'`. It concludes
`(hq.monodromy (FundamentalGroup.mapOfEq f h γ).asHom e' : F) =
g (hp.monodromy γ.asHom e)`. It does not require simple connectivity.
Its complete non-mathlib closure is only two new modules,
`Topology/Homotopy/Monodromy/Functoriality.lean` and `Logic/Function/Fiber.lean`:
428 lines / 20,159 bytes. This was proposed promptly, but root selected the
still smaller exact extraction and existing mathlib endpoint laws.

The full TauCeti fundamental-group `BasepointChange.lean` closure has ten
modules, 3,420 lines / 168,961 bytes, including five already vendored modules.
Five new modules would add 1,969 lines / 94,421 bytes; the extra homeomorphism,
conjugation and normalizer-quotient bookkeeping is not needed by the selected
two proofs. `Monodromy/BasepointChange.lean` would bring thirteen modules,
4,100 lines / 205,855 bytes, seven new. These full closures are not imported.

**FormalFrontier exact quotient naturality.** Its
`IsQuotientCoveringMap.fundamentalGroupToMulOpposite_naturality` assumes two
actual quotient coverings, a homomorphism `ρ : G →* H`, continuous total/base
maps `F,f`, `q ∘ F = f ∘ p`, and pointwise equivariance
`F (g • e) = ρ g • F e`. It proves equality of homomorphisms
`newMonodromy.comp (FundamentalGroup.map f x) =
(MonoidHom.op ρ).comp oldMonodromy`. The proof constructs monodromy naturality
from actual lifted path classes; no desired commutation is assumed as a field.
Its full closure is three new modules, 1,078 lines / 51,736 bytes, across the
two FormalFrontier repositories listed above. Its basepoint file also proves
`FundamentalGroup.mapOfEq_comp_fundamentalGroupMulEquivOfPath`, including the
correct endpoint casts; its full closure is two modules, 1,948 lines /
90,065 bytes. These are real candidates, but none was selected or compiled.

**Sphere-six endpoint transport.** The exact declaration
`SphereSixComplex.fundamentalGroupToMulOpposite_transport_endpoint` takes
`hp : IsQuotientCoveringMap p G`, `W : Path x y`, `ex : p ⁻¹' {x}` and
`γ : FundamentalGroup X x`, and asserts

```text
hp.fundamentalGroupToMulOpposite (hp.isCoveringMap.monodromy ⟦W⟧ ex)
  (FundamentalGroup.fundamentalGroupMulEquivOfPath W γ)
= hp.fundamentalGroupToMulOpposite ex γ.
```

This is exactly the compatible-lift transport shape, with no simply-connected
total-space assumption. The same file proves quotient-cover naturality from
a `QuotientCoverMapData` containing actual continuous maps, deck homomorphism,
commuting square and pointwise equivariance; the conclusion is not a field.
Its full imported affine/punctured-plane development was not audited or built,
so no full-closure reuse was proposed. The selected short path formula plus
existing mathlib monodromy laws supports the local M4 derivation directly.

## Reproduction and bounded search limits

The selected extraction is checked read-only from `sequences/` by
`python3 scripts/providers/assemble.py --check`. The actual verification
commands, each with retained raw output and exit status, were:

```bash
python3 scripts/providers/run_checks.py build
python3 scripts/providers/run_checks.py audit
python3 scripts/providers/run_checks.py replay
python3 scripts/providers/summarize.py
```

The replay invocation is the supported official
`lake env leanchecker --verbose ArtinSequenceVendor.FundamentalGroup.BasepointChange`.
No shared cache/dependency update or competing toolchain installation occurred.
Only the selected provider, its audit/tooling/evidence, and this task's
search documents/inventory were authored after root expanded the task scope.

The bounded GitHub code queries were `fundamentalGroupToMulOpposite`,
`fundamentalGroupMulEquivOfPath`, `monodromy naturality`, `mulEquivEnd`, and
`monodromy basepoint`, with `.lean` filtering and up to 100 indexed hits per
query. Results included mathlib/OpenAI duplicates; these were filtered during
candidate assessment, not mistaken for new suppliers. Query counts and all

The search cannot establish absence of another useful theorem in unindexed
branches or repositories. A hit, source appearance, `#check`, claimed no-`sorry`
status or successful build alone is never recorded as proof acceptance.

# Landmark 5: OpenAI source search and the remaining geometric bridge

This is a source-search report, **not acceptance of a new supplier or a proof of asphericity**. It continues the [earlier search](../search-openai.md) after landmarks 1–4. Its durable machine record is [m5-openai-inventory.json](../../provenance/searches/m5-openai-inventory.json). No scientific Lean source, provider, package configuration or cache was changed. No candidate was compiled, transitively axiom-audited or kernel-replayed in this search.

The inspected sources contain an ordinary Coxeter–Artin Salvetti contraction and useful generic poset contractions. I found no directly applicable theorem proving asphericity of the **actual restricted complexified arrangement complement**. The search was broader than the former 617-module closure; its precise coverage and limits appear below. This does not assert absence from every repository, branch or possible theorem terminology.

## Pins, licensing and reproducible coverage

A fresh GitHub `commits/main` query returned `4eaee87548250b2682affda7d05d947c05554bae`, dated `2026-10-30T00:35:35Z`, identical to the previously inspected openai/math pin. Thus current `main` supplied no newer version of these proofs. Other branches and tags were not exhaustively searched. The fetched immutable configuration specifies Lean `v4.34.1`, mathlib `d13f23b723b8a846827a245b89c10fc7d3f11612`, and Apache-2.0 licensing. This is not the project's current toolchain; source discovery does not establish compatibility.

The inventory records source URLs, SHA-256 hashes, Git blob identities, direct imports, literal selected declaration headers, context/hypotheses, closure coverage and disposition. Every inspected Lean source for which a complete subtree supplied a blob identity matched that identity. The following complete recursive subtree inventories were searched; entry counts include directories.

| Subtree under `lean/OAI` | Tree SHA | Entries |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| `Topology` | `7ea0275d387dc5545a3cd288cde98fa1bfc550d1` | 1311 |
| `Topology/ArtinGroups` | `0b8f7c175022e4696404bb2bbabf12746f899d14` | 891 |
| `AlgebraicTopology` | `379be79523387a94d775f0f6939de4db951ad44d` | 644 |
| `Geometry` | `b0a9be666fb8dfdecda3add9b0d0044374a123a7` | 14720 |
| `GroupTheory` | `7f009e658de6eaaa769ffd2a733f6e8d4ec059f4` | 4239 |
| `Combinatorics` | `b45090b6d5bc04e0962f2c7547b1e4643a5dd1a1` | 16844 |
| `Dynamics` | `3ac4ebd40bdd3f03b13f47975716f8edcacda2e9` | 680 |

All **1288 Topology Lean source bodies** were machine-screened with the recorded patterns: all 881 ArtinGroups files, including 264 outside the earlier closure, and all 407 remaining Topology files. Individual proof bodies were read for the candidates described below; machine screening is not full manual proof reading. Outside Topology, complete subtree **paths** were searched and selected bodies fetched/read. The root recursive tree is truncated, so it was not used to infer exhaustive repository coverage. The existing exact-pin comparison with `mathcommunity/oai-math-revised` (`d25fae85c2f5ce5aadac40fb2b4c2d332b393d1c`) establishes identical relevant old subtrees; this search did not freshly query revised's latest branch.

The ordinary `SalvettiProjection` OAI import closure was independently recomputed from actual sources: exactly the same **617** modules as the old inventory, with no missing OAI source. The selected `SalvettiCoverContractible` closure has 602 modules. Closure completeness is a source fact, not successful compilation or an axiom audit. Previously accepted algebraic providers do not certify this larger topology closure.

## What the ordinary Salvetti endpoints actually say

Names in this subsection are in `OAI.HarmonicArtin`, at the immutable [ArtinGroups source directory](https://github.com/openai/math/tree/4eaee87548250b2682affda7d05d947c05554bae/lean/OAI/Topology/ArtinGroups).

`Model.lean` defines the actual braid-presented `Artin M`, `IsSpherical M T := Finite (coxeterParabolic M T)`, and `LiftedCell M := Artin M × SphericalType M`. Its face relation uses ordinary Coxeter reduced words and minimal coset representatives. The cover is literally

```lean
noncomputable def SalvettiCover (M : CoxeterMatrix S) : TopCat :=
  SSet.toTop.obj (CategoryTheory.nerve (LiftedCell M))
```

`Realizations/SalvettiCoverContractible.lean` states, for arbitrary universe `S : Type u`:

```lean
theorem salvetti_cover_contractible [Finite S] (M : CoxeterMatrix S) :
    ContractibleSpace (SalvettiCover M)
```

This is an unconditional **finite-rank ordinary** statement, without a finite-W premise. The full proof closure has not been newly accepted here. Its exact breadth is recorded rather than silently narrowing its hypotheses.

`Realizations/CellUnion.lean` constructs `SourceSalvetti M` as a quotient of spherical Coxeter cell points by explicit face identifications, with the quotient topology. It proves a homeomorphism to the ordinary deck quotient. `Realizations/SalvettiProjection.lean`, under `[Fintype S] [DecidableEq S]`, gives a genuine covering projection `SalvettiCover M → SourceSalvetti M`, its surjectivity, contractible/simply connected source, and

```lean
sourceFundamentalGroupEquiv (x : SourceSalvetti M) :
  FundamentalGroup (SourceSalvetti M) x ≃* Artin M
```

The basepoint is in **SourceSalvetti**, not the actual relative complement. No relative set `J`, restricted arrangement on its flat, or normalizer action occurs in these definitions. `restricted_lifted_contractible` in `RestrictedLiftedContractible.lean` concerns an ordinary standard parabolic matrix `restrictedMatrix M T`; the word “restricted” does not mean the restricted arrangement of the paper. Similarly, `DeligneRealization M` is the nerve of ordinary spherical Artin cosets.

The relative arrangement generally is not a Coxeter arrangement for a new matrix, and its normalizer quotient need not act transitively on chambers. Therefore selecting a new matrix does not instantiate these endpoints. A new actual higher-homotopy comparison would be necessary even if this entire supplier closure passed technical validation. Landmark 3's fundamental-groupoid equivalence controls the 1-type; it supplies no higher-homotopy comparison by itself.

## Generic tools found beyond that endpoint

The literal selected headers and context are in the JSON inventory; this table describes their practical use and limits.

| Supplier | Genuine conclusion and inputs | Disposition for M5 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Realizations/DirectedCoverSequence.lean`, `orderWeights_contractible_of_countable_directed_cover` | Contractibility of `OrderWeights P`, from a countable nonempty directed cover by **downward closed** subposets whose realizations are contractible, plus a bounded strictly monotone natural-number rank | Useful potential combinatorial tool. It does not contract actual open subsets of a lifted complement. Its OAI closure has 105 modules. |
| `OrderWeightsContractibleLower.lean`, `orderWeights_contractible_of_lower_fibers` | Contracts a poset realization from an already contractible subposet, contractible lower fibers outside it, and bounded strict rank | Potential attachment lemma; 28 OAI modules. The fibers must actually be proved contractible. |
| `OrderWeightsContractibleLower2.lean`, `orderWeights_contractible_of_lower_preimages` | An order-map criterion using contractible target/lower preimages and rank bounds on both posets | Potential comparison tool; 103 OAI modules. No geometric complement map is supplied. |
| `Topology/Euclidean/IncreasingCover.lean`, `...Globalization.exists_compact_subset_increasing_cover` | Every compact set in a monotone open cover lies in one member | The proof directly applies mathlib `IsCompact.elim_directed_cover`. Prefer that existing theorem over this file's unrelated singular-homology dependencies. |
| `Topology/Homotopy/CubicalNullity.lean`, `OAI.NearbyLagrangian.CubicalFreeNullity.null_of_moving_base` | For finite nonempty cubical dimension, converts an actual free nullhomotopy whose boundary is a moving point into a based `GenLoop` nullhomotopy | Small candidate importing only `Mathlib`. It could finish a genuine compact-image contraction argument; it provides no such geometric contraction. Not yet accepted or compiled here. |
| `Topology/Homotopy/RayTelescope.lean`, `...exists_finite_representative`, `...stage_nullhomotopic_iff` | Compact maps/homotopies into an explicit quotient ray telescope have finite-stage representatives; nullhomotopy can be checked eventually | Imports only `Mathlib`, but its space is a telescope, not the actual lifted complement. A homotopy comparison would remain necessary. |
| `GroupTheory/FiniteType/CWWhitehead.lean`, `OAI.CWWhitehead.contractible_subtype` | Contracts an actual nonempty CW subspace given `CWCylinder.SphereFill` for that space | Cannot supply the missing sphere-filling premise. Its external OAI closure was not fetched completely here. Direct higher-homotopy vanishing avoids requiring this stronger CW conclusion. |

`OrderWeights P` is substantive: finitely supported nonnegative real weights, total weight one, support a chain, and topology coinduced from actual nerve-simplex charts. It is not an artificial contractibility field. Nevertheless, its contraction is a theorem about this realization. Relating that realization to the actual lifted complement remains a mathematical obligation.

The additional Artin module `ParabolicIntersections/RelativeLowerContractible.lean` was read in full. Its `relativeAllEligibleLower_contractible` contracts a harmonic-height/link subposet of the **ordinary** Deligne coset poset, with distinguished-generator, support and cutoff hypotheses. It is not a theorem about restricted real hyperplanes. Other nearby `relative`/`normalizer` hits are ordinary group/poset constructions.

The broader path/body search also found several misleadingly adjacent names:

- `Dynamics/EntropyCounterexample/CoordinateGoodCover.lean` defines legitimate open-cover data with contractible nonempty finite intersections and explicitly contracts sphere slices. Its constructions concern spheres/manifolds. It does not prove a generic nerve homotopy theorem. `RawBaseGoodCover.lean` transports one such example through homeomorphisms.
- `Geometry/SingularHomology/FiniteGoodCoverHomology.lean` proves finite-dimensionality/eventual vanishing of **homology** through algebraic gluing. `TetrahedronGoodCoverBundle.lean` constructs a good cover of a tetrahedral sphere. Neither proves the needed arrangement asphericity or actual nerve equivalence.
- `GroupTheory/SimpleAmenable/Simplicial/BarContractible.lean` supplies positive-degree simplicial **homology** vanishing for special bar constructions. Its filename does not establish topological contractibility of a general Garside category.
- `AlgebraicTopology/Cohomology/Singular/ChartLocalContractible.lean` proves local contractibility of charted spaces. Local contractibility alone says nothing about the global higher homotopy groups in question.

## Faithful remaining proof route

I read the archived original Deligne extracted text at 2.14–2.15 and 3.7A–D (printed pp.290–296), not the whole original paper or a fresh visual PDF. Reviewer A separately reports complete visual reading of §§1–3. The archived PDF has SHA-256 `1905043232e1dadd97696372252bb5f91c202ea1b72379e77a9fecbfe9eed4bc`; its source is [Deligne, *Les immeubles des groupes de tresses généralisés*](https://publications.ias.edu/sites/default/files/Number18.pdf). See [contract A](milestone5-contract-a.md) for the independently reviewed complete route and [contract B](milestone5-contract-b.md) for the exact final theorem scope.

A useful decomposition is:

1. **Actual simplicial arrangement.** Transport the off-parabolic coordinate basis through the existing actual facet/flat maps, proving each actual chamber is the strictly positive cone of a basis. Prove the finite retained forms span the flat when essentiality is needed. Keep duplicate forms harmless. This is concrete geometry, with no topological asphericity conclusion.
2. **Signed combinatorial cover and contraction.** Build the actual positive/signed chamber complex using the proved chamber/ribbon data. Prove its face identifications and the positive length-filtration attachments. Deligne 2.9 contracts the positive complex; 2.14 exhausts the signed one by translated positive complexes; 2.15 concludes contractibility. Generic OAI order-realization lemmas might reduce this work after an actual poset and its rank/fibers are established. The ordinary coset complex cannot simply be renamed.
3. **Actual geometric cover.** Construct a covering of the actual complement by gluing actual tube sheets with the signed chamber transition data, or use an independently proved actual universal covering construction. Prove the local evenly covered neighborhoods; Deligne 3.7A uses facet-star neighborhoods. A mere definition of a covering candidate is insufficient.
4. **Actual higher-topology bridge.** Deligne 3.7B–D refines to a vertex/face-indexed open cover, identifies its nerve with the combinatorial cover, and proves nonempty finite intersections contractible. Intersections containing a chamber center have affine contractions (3.7.5). Other face intersections compare, via an actual pullback and homotopy equivalence, to lower-rank localized lifted arrangements (3.7.7–3.7.8); induction finishes them. One must then prove/use a genuine topological nerve homotopy theorem. Existing tube contractions and the Čech theorem for fundamental **groupoids** do not replace this step.
5. **Higher vanishing and transfer.** Contractibility of the actual covering space implies its higher homotopy groups vanish; covering transfer gives actual complement asphericity, then the already proved quotient covering gives orbit-space asphericity. Combine the actual M4 group equivalences and commuting sequences with the K(π,1) definitions at arbitrary actual basepoints. No new normalizer/group identification is needed here.

A potentially smaller alternative to steps 2–4 is to construct a **directed open exhaustion of the actual simply connected cover whose members have actual nullhomotopic inclusions**, or actual contractions. Compact cubical maps then land in one member by `IsCompact.elim_directed_cover`, and free-to-based nullity gives higher vanishing. This avoids a full CW/Whitehead conclusion and may avoid a global nerve theorem. The decisive new proof is still geometric: the exhaustion members and their contractions/nullhomotopic inclusions must be constructed from Deligne's positive filtration and actual lifted overlaps. Contractibility of arbitrary finite unions of lifted tubes is not a consequence of individual tube contractibility. Their intersections can be disconnected. No inspected OpenAI endpoint supplies this filtration theorem.

A generic Garside classifying-space theorem would have the same limitation unless its actual space is connected to the complement by a proved higher-homotopy equivalence. Likewise the restricted complement lies in ambient reflecting hyperplanes, so it is not simply the ambient regular Coxeter complement with a convenient fixed-point subgroup. A new fixed-point/stratum comparison would need its own proof.

The first inexpensive independently authorable obligations are the flat-coordinate/simpliciality statement, and the generic compact-directed-open-cover higher-nullity lemma. The former discharges a genuine Deligne hypothesis; the latter isolates a small topological endpoint. Neither should be advertised as the full geometric Deligne theorem. Rank zero/full `J` must remain included: the actual flat/complement is a point and the retained arrangement is empty. Any positive-dimensional/spherical convention in a supplier must have a separate zero-dimensional case. Arbitrary `J`, reducible and noncrystallographic finite Coxeter groups remain in scope.

## Execution and claim limits

This search used read-only source/hash/GitHub queries, plus writes to this report and its machine inventory. Full-source keyword coverage and exact import-closure recovery are recorded; they are not kernel validation. No inference is made from a README, theorem name, CI badge, or homology-only conclusion to actual asphericity. No desired contraction, geometric comparison, or asphericity is proposed as an assumed field in a completed theorem.

# Landmark 5: other GitHub supplier search

Research date: 2026-11-14. Project baseline:
`22301de0ff626dbfb3d8ae66a6bccc50317de702`.
This report and the [durable machine inventory](../../provenance/searches/m5-other-inventory.json)
are the only project files changed by this task. No candidate was imported,
built, axiom-audited, kernel-replayed, independently reviewed, or accepted.
**No third-party proof was used in the formalization by this search.**

## Decision

No directly applicable Deligne theorem for the actual complexified complement
of a finite central simplicial real arrangement was found in this bounded
search outside mathlib, TauCeti, and openai/math. There are substantive
generic topology candidates in **kangxyz/colib** and its predecessor
**kangxyz/quillen-k-theory**:

- Genuine groupoid nerve realizations have trivial higher homotopy groups.
- Actual partition-of-unity and interpolation maps give domination by an
  actual cover nerve, under explicit local geometric hypotheses.
- Filtered simplicial colimits preserve actual stage homotopy equivalences
  when the canonical transition maps satisfy the stated hypotheses.

These are potentially useful prerequisites. None supplies the missing
arrangement-specific higher-homotopy comparison or contractibility argument.
Immediate reuse is not recommended merely to collect an asphericity-shaped
endpoint; first identify its exact role in a proof about the actual space.

The target remains `Theorem18.Complement M J`, the actual subspace of
`relativeSubspace J × relativeSubspace J` obtained by removing simultaneous
zeros of the retained real root forms, and its actual normalizer orbit space.
Landmark 3's equivalence of fundamental groupoids controls path classes.
It does not identify higher homotopy groups with those of a groupoid nerve.

## Immutable positive candidates and their cost

| Repository | Inspected commit | Toolchain | mathlib pin | License |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [kangxyz/colib](https://github.com/kangxyz/colib/tree/bac5cab53eb6526e366e861d289253ec81aa89f0) | `bac5cab53eb6526e366e861d289253ec81aa89f0` | Lean `v4.35.0` | `56a005855ea17e0b0958f73ec801ae140b0a1679` | Apache-2.0 |
| [kangxyz/quillen-k-theory](https://github.com/kangxyz/quillen-k-theory/tree/c561118b7795eb9780be9ed391c3251d6a4d0afd) | `c561118b7795eb9780be9ed391c3251d6a4d0afd` | Lean `v4.34.1` | `d13f23b723b8a846827a245b89c10fc7d3f11612` | Apache-2.0 |

Both pinned root license files were read and hashed. Colib explicitly
attributes the relevant implementations to the above Quillen revision;
these are related developments, not independent confirmations. Neither
toolchain/mathlib pair matches this project's `v4.36.0-rc2` /
`65d730f7150f21fdfa32f3e73a3f549c1f96a0e9`. Compatibility is untested.

Counts below include the requested root and all transitively imported
repository modules, excluding Mathlib and standard tool dependencies. Lines
include comments and blanks. The machine inventory contains every file hash
and import edge, not just these totals.

| Root suffix after `Colib.` or `Quillen.` | Colib modules / lines | Quillen modules / lines |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `Topology.ClassifyingSpace.Groupoid` | 259 / 38,583 | 236 / 37,536 |
| `Topology.Realization.NumerableRealizationDomination` | 18 / 2,123 | 17 / 2,573 |
| `Topology.Realization.MetricRealizationDomination` | 21 / 2,372 | 20 / 2,807 |
| `Topology.FilteredRealization.HomotopyEquivalence` | 74 / 9,731 | 102 / 15,155 |

All Colib closures above have no further third-party mathematical import
beyond Mathlib. The Quillen groupoid and filtered-realization closures also
import `Aglib.CategoryTheory.ExactCategory.Basic`, from
**kangxyz/aglib**, commit `2c34f185fa859e862661f939cd216b07bcccfb26`,
Apache-2.0. Its actual source closure is one additional file, 207 lines,
with Mathlib imports. Thus the complete non-Mathlib groupoid cohort is
237 modules / 37,743 lines for that predecessor. This extra dependency
must not be omitted from a proposed reuse record.

### Actual groupoid realizations

[`Colib/Topology/ClassifyingSpace/Basic.lean`](https://github.com/kangxyz/colib/blob/bac5cab53eb6526e366e861d289253ec81aa89f0/Colib/Topology/ClassifyingSpace/Basic.lean)
defines, in namespace `CategoryTheory`,

```lean
def ClassifyingSpace (C : Type u) [Category.{v} C] : TopCat.{max u v} :=
  SSet.toTop.obj (CategoryTheory.nerve C)
```

Its points and topology are the actual geometric realization. The
[`Groupoid.lean`](https://github.com/kangxyz/colib/blob/bac5cab53eb6526e366e861d289253ec81aa89f0/Colib/Topology/ClassifyingSpace/Groupoid.lean)
endpoint, in namespace `CategoryTheory.GroupoidClassifying`, is

```lean
variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [IsGroupoid C]
theorem subsingleton_higher_pi_at (x : ClassifyingSpace C) (n : ℕ) :
  Subsingleton (HomotopyGroup.Pi (n + 2) (ClassifyingSpace C) x)
```

The proof is substantive. The actual comma category of a point inclusion
is equivalent to the discrete set of original arrows. Theorem B compares
its realization with the actual homotopy fiber; the long exact sequence
then kills higher homotopy at vertices, and actual paths from arbitrary
realization points to vertices transport the result. The imported
`HomotopyFiber` definition was checked: it is the actual subtype

```lean
{z : X × C(I, Y) // z.2 0 = f z.1 ∧ z.2 1 = y}
```

with inherited topology. The conclusion uses mathlib's genuine
`HomotopyGroup.Pi`, not a newly defined vanishing invariant.

The predecessor endpoint is
`Quillen.GroupoidClassifying.subsingleton_higher_pi_at`, with the same
geometric domain. All-point, arbitrary-universe statements are explicit;
no arrangement, Artin, or simpliciality hypothesis appears.

**Missing bridge:** a suitable actual higher-homotopy comparison between
the complement and this realization. A categorical equivalence
`IntervalGroupoid ≌ FundamentalGroupoid (Complement M J)` cannot discharge
that bridge. Instantiating `C` with either of those groupoids establishes
asphericity of its classifying space, not of the original complement.

### Constructed cover-nerve domination

The Colib namespace is `Topology.NumerableConnectorCover`; the predecessor
uses `Quillen.NumerableConnectorCover`. The actual
[`LocalEquiconnection`](https://github.com/kangxyz/colib/blob/bac5cab53eb6526e366e861d289253ec81aa89f0/Colib/Topology/LocalEquiconnection.lean)
has an open neighborhood of the diagonal in `A × A`, a continuous connector
on that domain times the interval, its two endpoint equations, and a
diagonal-fixing equation. It contains no realization comparison or desired
domination as a field. Connector-convexity requires pairs to lie in this
domain and their interpolations to remain in the specified set.

The numerable theorem has actual data

```lean
E : LocalEquiconnection A
W : ι → Set A
V : κ → Set A
hconvex : ∀ k, E.IsConvex (V k)
href : PointStarRefines W V
hcover : ∀ x, ∃ i, x ∈ W i
vertex : ι → A
hvertex : ∀ i, vertex i ∈ W i
ρ : PartitionOfUnity ι A
hρ : ρ.IsSubordinate W
```

and a linear order on the index type. `PointStarRefines` means
`∀ x, ∃ k, {y | ∃ i, x ∈ W i ∧ y ∈ W i} ⊆ V k`.
Its actual ordered nerve is the simplicial subcomplex of the order nerve
whose vertex lists have a common point in their cover members.

[`exists_numerable_realization_domination`](https://github.com/kangxyz/colib/blob/bac5cab53eb6526e366e861d289253ec81aa89f0/Colib/Topology/Realization/NumerableRealizationDomination.lean)
constructs

```lean
∃ (K : SSet.{v}) (a : C(A, |K|)) (b : C(|K|, A)),
  Nonempty ((b.comp a).Homotopy (ContinuousMap.id A))
```

The displayed proof selects the actual ordered nerve and the constructed
`partitionNerveMap` and `nerveReturnMap`. The classifier uses original
partition coefficients; finite support charts prove continuity into the
weak realization. The return map uses ordered connector interpolation,
with face compatibility and degenerate-coordinate aggregation proved
before descending through the simplicial colimit. The connector constructs
the displayed composite homotopy.

The metric variant
`exists_metric_realization_domination` assumes a metric on `A`, the local
connector, and an open connector-convex cover. Its proof constructs a
positive radius, point-star-refining small balls, and a subordinate partition
using metric paracompactness. It supplies the same domination conclusion.

**Missing bridge:** the returned nerve is not identified with the desired
Deligne/Salvetti complex or an aspherical groupoid realization. Only the
composite on `A` is made homotopic to the identity; the theorem does not
claim a two-sided nerve equivalence. Even applying it to the actual open
arrangement complement would still require proving higher-homotopy
vanishing of an appropriate constructed nerve. It is also not a general
component-good-cover theorem for the existing chamber tubes.

### Filtered realization and contractible cones

[`Topology.FilteredRealization.stageHomotopyEquiv`](https://github.com/kangxyz/colib/blob/bac5cab53eb6526e366e861d289253ec81aa89f0/Colib/Topology/FilteredRealization/HomotopyEquivalence.lean)
has these literal inputs:

```lean
{J : Type u} [SmallCategory J] [IsFiltered J]
F : J ⥤ SSet.{u}
c : Cocone F
hc : IsColimit c
e : ∀ {j k : J} (u : j ⟶ k), ContinuousMap.HomotopyEquiv |F.obj j| |F.obj k|
he : ∀ {j k : J} (u : j ⟶ k),
  (e u).toFun = (SSet.toTop.map (F.map u)).hom
```

It constructs `ContinuousMap.HomotopyEquiv |F.obj j| |c.pt|` with the
canonical cocone leg as its forward map. This is actual filtered-colimit
homotopy invariance. It is not, by itself, contractibility of the nerve
of an arbitrary filtered category. A concrete diagram and the required
transition homotopy equivalences still have to be proved.

Colib also has actual nerve contractions from an initial or terminal
object in `Topology/ClassifyingSpace/Contraction.lean` (19-module /
2,375-line closure). Those hypotheses could contract explicit finite cones;
they do not assert that a filtered category has a terminal object.
`GroupCompletionContractibleUniversal.lean` was also inspected: it assumes
contractibility of the classifying space of the acted-on category `D`
before proving contractibility of its particular localization. It is not
a generic Garside-category K(π,1) theorem with those hypotheses discharged.

## Coverage, execution limits, and next obligation

The durable inventory contains all 14 recorded queries, their returned
paths and exact blob revisions, all 36 repositories encountered (including
the transitive Aglib supplier), selected-source hashes, pinned topology
toolchains/manifests/licenses, and complete candidate import DAGs. There
are 35 repositories among the query hits; many were left as uninspected

results; all raw hits were retained and the body-inspection scope was
applied separately. OAI/TauCeti hits remain recorded without being treated
as other-repository proofs.

Complete immutable trees were obtained for Quillen (8,458 entries) and

were inspected. All candidate closure modules were hashed, their imports
traversed, and their source text screened after removing nested comments
for `sorry`, `admit`, `native_decide`, and custom `axiom` declarations;
no matches were found in those closures. This is not a compiled transitive
axiom audit and does not establish closure correctness. Most imported
proof bodies were not independently reviewed line by line. For negative
candidates only relevant definition/endpoint/proof segments were read;
their unrelated closures were not accepted or exhaustively inspected.

Searches for Salvetti, Garside, simplicial/Deligne arrangements, good covers,
nerve comparison, filtered nerves, and asphericity support a bounded reuse
decision. Empty queries and name-based scans do not establish worldwide
absence of a formal theorem. No toolchain installation, build, cache
operation, vendor change, or scientific-source change was performed.

The concrete remaining bridge is a higher-dimensional geometric comparison
for the actual arrangement, followed by a Deligne/Garside contractibility
argument for its actual covering model. The existing component/groupoid
comparison cannot replace that argument. Once an exact useful topology
endpoint is selected for this route, its complete immutable source cohort
must undergo local compilation, axiom and physical-declaration coverage,
exact-module replay, and independent statement review before reuse.

# Landmark 5: TauCeti, mathlib, and bounded supplementary GitHub search

Search snapshot: 2026-11-14. Project baseline: `22301de0ff626dbfb3d8ae66a6bccc50317de702`.
Machine inventory: [`m5-tauceti-inventory.json`](../../provenance/searches/m5-tauceti-inventory.json).

## Result and scope

The inspected sources supply genuine higher-homotopy definitions, covering transfer, an actual path-class universal cover, and compactness tools. This search did **not** establish asphericity of the actual finite central simplicial arrangement complement, an actual comparison with a contractible Deligne complex, or a directed contractible-open exhaustion of its universal cover. These are the outstanding geometric inputs. This is a bounded source search, not a claim that no external proof exists.

At the initial search stage no new proof/module was imported, copied, built, axiom-audited, kernel-replayed, or accepted. Root subsequently selected the 11-module topology cohort described below for actual staging and verification; acceptance remains a separate step. Existing accepted vendor APIs are distinguished below from unselected source candidates. Prior acceptance is recorded in `vendor/theorem18-provenance.json`; that earlier evidence was consulted, not freshly rerun here. A source-inspected candidate is not formally verified by this report.

The existing M3 equivalence of the interval groupoid with the fundamental groupoid of the actual complement supplies information about paths and their homotopy classes. It does not imply vanishing of higher homotopy groups. The actual complement remains the subtype in `ArtinNormalisers/Theorem18/Geometry.lean`, with the inherited topology and the condition that no retained relative root vanishes on both real coordinates; it is not replaced by a classifying space.

## Pins and licenses

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `leanprover-community/mathlib4` | `65d730f7150f21fdfa32f3e73a3f549c1f96a0e9` | Project Lean `v4.36.0-rc2` | Apache-2.0; existing dependency, no update. |
| `TauCetiProject/TauCeti` | `62bbc0596dc3539d488232e4e924a338548ea0a9` | Lean `v4.36.0-rc2`; upstream mathlib `e8ba86fa9744dd8d90f48c1752bc735f61a4ca81` | Apache-2.0; existing selected closure plus unselected candidates. |
| `TauCetiProject/TauCeti` latest comparison | `130523811f55c80f533e6024e190b945755f93c5` | Same Lean and upstream mathlib pins | Apache-2.0; five relevant files compared byte-for-byte with the old pin and unchanged. |
| `zstone1/Cubical` | `5339856b84db66f7ba3b831c00d40264447b8d21` | Lean `v4.30.0`; mathlib `c5ea00351c28e24afc9f0f84379aa41082b1188f` | No LICENSE/COPYING path found in inspected tracked tree; no copying proposed. Combinatorial category comparison only. |
| `Arthur742Ramos/ComputationalPathsLean` | `257c659b7973aeda900d86a5da73b208712c7523` | Lean `v4.33.0`; mathlib `db584cd6d46c92f209a44c0f1c829460d327499d` | MIT; inspected nerve interfaces do not prove a topological nerve theorem. |

Exact source SHA256s, import lists, selected metadata files, read limits, search-hit repositories, failures and dispositions are preserved in the machine inventory. Search-hit-only repositories were not source-read, used, or verified; their pins are those in returned GitHub blob URLs, not inferred current HEADs.

## The actual all-degree property already available

`vendor/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/EilenbergMacLane/Basic.lean` defines:

```lean
def TauCeti.IsAspherical (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] (x : X) : Prop :=
  PathConnectedSpace X ∧ ∀ n, Subsingleton (π_ (n + 2) X x)

def TauCeti.IsEilenbergMacLaneSpaceOne (G : Type*) [Group G]
    (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] (x : X) : Prop :=
  IsAspherical X x ∧ Nonempty (FundamentalGroup X x ≃* G)
```

Here mathlib's generalized loops are actual continuous maps from the cube `(N → unitInterval)` to `X`, sending its boundary `{y | ∃ i, y i = 0 ∨ y i = 1}` to the basepoint. `π_ n` is the quotient by homotopy relative to that boundary, using `Fin n`. Thus the first predicate quantifies over every dimension at least two. It is not just a statement about π₁, π₂, a discrete groupoid, or an assumed classifying-space equivalence.

The unselected `TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/EilenbergMacLane/Degree.lean:57` additionally defines:

```lean
IsEilenbergMacLaneSpace G n X x :=
  PathConnectedSpace X ∧
  (∀ k, k ≠ 0 → k ≠ n → Subsingleton (π_ k X x)) ∧
  Nonempty (π_ n X x ≃* G)
```

It requires `[NeZero n]`; at degree one, its theorem `isEilenbergMacLaneSpace_one_iff` relates this to the existing degree-one predicate. This is a definition/packaging API, not a proof of arrangement asphericity. Literal degree definition and surrounding main APIs were read; the entire file was not proof-reviewed.

Mathlib `Topology/Homotopy/Contractible.lean:52` defines `ContractibleSpace X` by `Nonempty (X ≃ₕ Unit)`, and provides `id_nullhomotopic`. The hypothesis is a genuine contraction up to continuous homotopy equivalence, not a marker field.

## Already selected covering-transfer APIs

The existing 23-module higher-homotopy supplier closure rooted at `TauCeti.AlgebraicTopology.EilenbergMacLane.Covering` is recorded as 305,059 bytes in the existing provenance. Its exact inspected useful declarations are:

| Declaration | Essential hypotheses and conclusion | Actual application |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `IsCoveringMap.homotopyGroupPiMulEquiv` | `(hp : IsCoveringMap p) (e : E) (n : ℕ)` gives `π_ (n+2) E e ≃* π_ (n+2) X (p e)` | Transfer genuine higher-homotopy vanishing across an actual cover. |
| `IsCoveringMap.isAspherical` | `hp`, `Surjective p`, `he : p e = x`, `IsAspherical E e` give `IsAspherical X x` | Once the actual complement is aspherical, transfer to the already constructed orbit quotient cover. |
| `IsCoveringMap.isAspherical_totalSpace` | `hp`, `[PathConnectedSpace E]`, `he`, `IsAspherical X x` give `IsAspherical E e` | Reverse transfer if a useful aspherical base becomes available. |
| `IsCoveringMap.isAspherical_of_subsingleton_homotopyGroup` | `hp`, surjectivity, `[PathConnectedSpace E]`, `he`, and `∀n, Subsingleton (π_(n+2) E e)` | Sufficient for the proposed actual-universal-cover route. |
| `IsQuotientCoveringMap.isEilenbergMacLaneSpaceOne` | actual quotient cover, `[SimplyConnectedSpace E]`, basepoint equation, and all higher groups of `E` trivial | Packages a K(G,1) only after the real covering and higher vanishing are proved. |
| `TauCeti.IsEilenbergMacLaneSpaceOne.mk` | actual asphericity and `Nonempty (FundamentalGroup X x ≃* G)` | Combine new asphericity with M4's actual group equivalence. |

The `IsQuotientCoveringMap` theorem must not be applied to `Complement → OrbitComplement` using a simply-connectedness hypothesis that has not been proved for `Complement`.

## A genuine universal-cover candidate

Pinned `TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/UniversalCover/Basic.lean` constructs

```lean
structure TauCeti.UniversalCover (x₀ : X) where
  proj : X
  path : Path.Homotopic.Quotient x₀ proj
```

Its topology is coinduced from `ofBasedPath x₀`. `BasedPath x₀ := {γ : C(unitInterval, X) // γ 0 = x₀}` has the compact-open subspace topology; the construction is not a discrete sigma topology. It contains an actual constant-path basepoint, and `range_proj x₀ = pathComponent x₀`. For the actual path-connected complement this yields surjectivity of the endpoint map.

Pinned `UniversalCover/Covering.lean:51,116,183` proves:

```lean
UniversalCover.isCoveringMap
  [LocallyPathConnectedSpace X] [TauCeti.SemilocallySimplyConnectedSpace X]
  (x₀ : X) : IsCoveringMap (UniversalCover.proj (x₀ := x₀))

UniversalCover.pathConnectedSpace (x₀ : X) :
  PathConnectedSpace (TauCeti.UniversalCover x₀)

UniversalCover.simplyConnectedSpace
  [LocallyPathConnectedSpace X] [TauCeti.SemilocallySimplyConnectedSpace X]
  (x₀ : X) : SimplyConnectedSpace (TauCeti.UniversalCover x₀)
```

The path-connectedness construction needs no local assumptions. Simple connectedness is proved through actual path lifting and cancellation in endpoint-preserving path-homotopy classes. The covering construction allows empty fibers off the basepoint path component; surjectivity still needs path connectedness of the base. `existsUnique_continuousMap_lifts` is the actual universal lifting property for continuous maps from simply connected, locally path-connected spaces. No `UniversalCover/Construction.lean` or `UniversalCover/SimplyConnected.lean` exists at this pin: the relevant implementation is `BasedPath`, `Basic`, `Covering`.

A recursive import walk gives 13 TauCeti files / 193,800 bytes. Five are already vendored; the eight new files total 119,260 bytes / 2,242 lines:

- `AlgebraicTopology/UniversalCover/{BasedPath,Basic,Covering}.lean`
- `AlgebraicTopology/SemilocallySimplyConnected/{Basic,On}.lean`
- `Topology/Homotopy/TubeNeighborhood.lean`
- `Topology/IsLocalHomeomorph.lean`
- `Topology/SeparatedMap.lean`

The complete path/hash/import inventory is embedded in the JSON. Full `BasedPath`, `Covering`, and semilocal `Basic` were read; universal-cover `Basic` definitions/topology and declaration inventory were read, not every proof. Other closure modules were import-walked, not individually proof-reviewed. At the initial search stage this candidate had not been compiled against the project's different mathlib pin. The subsequent selected-cohort section records the real build and audit.

### Local hypotheses for the actual complement

Unselected pinned `TauCeti/Topology/Algebra/Module/LocallyContractible.lean` is 43 lines, with only mathlib imports. It proves the instance

```lean
TauCeti.RealTopologicalVectorSpace.stronglyLocallyContractibleSpace
  [AddCommGroup E] [Module ℝ E] [TopologicalSpace E]
  [ContinuousAdd E] [ContinuousSMul ℝ E] : StronglyLocallyContractibleSpace E
```

Mathlib `IsOpen.stronglyLocallyContractibleSpace` transfers this to the actual open complement (`Theorem18.isOpen_complementSet`). Mathlib then supplies `LocallyPathConnectedSpace`; semilocal `Basic` supplies `SemilocallySimplyConnectedSpace` from strong local contractibility. Alternatively, the latter file's `of_forall_exists_mem_nhds_isSimplyConnected` derives semilocal simple connectivity from actual simply-connected neighborhood witnesses. An open contractible tube containing each point is sufficient for that semilocal condition; it is not by itself a proof that such tubes form a neighborhood basis. Full 43-line source and semilocal constructor were read.

### Compact directed-cover route

Pinned mathlib `Topology/Compactness/Compact.lean:188` proves exactly:

```lean
IsCompact.elim_directed_cover [Nonempty ι] (hs : IsCompact s)
  (U : ι → Set X) (hUo : ∀ i, IsOpen (U i))
  (hsU : s ⊆ ⋃ i, U i) (hdU : Directed (· ⊆ ·) U) :
  ∃ i, s ⊆ U i
```

For a finite-dimensional cube representative, continuity and compactness put its entire image in one member of an actual directed open cover. If that member is contractible and contains the basepoint, the representative factors through its subtype as a based generalized loop. Triviality of that subtype's homotopy group and functoriality of the inclusion imply triviality of the original class.

The directly relevant unselected pinned module `TauCeti/Topology/Homotopy/HomotopyGroup/HomotopyEquiv.lean` supplies:

```lean
HomotopyGroup.subsingleton_of_contractibleSpace
  [Finite N] [ContractibleSpace X] : Subsingleton (HomotopyGroup N X x)

HomotopyGroup.map_eq_one_of_nullhomotopic
  [Finite N] [Nonempty N] [DecidableEq N]
  {f : C(X, Y)} (hf : f.Nullhomotopic) (hfx : f x = y)
  (a : HomotopyGroup N X x) : HomotopyGroup.map f hfx a = 1
```

Its recursive TauCeti closure has 13 files, only two new relative to the current vendor tree: this 302-line module and `Topology/Homotopy/HomotopyEquiv.lean` (196 lines). Both were fully read. No CW assumption is present in this route. The missing input remains the actual directed contractible-open cover of the actual universal cover; arbitrary unions of lifted contractible tubes are not automatically contractible. No such theorem was found in the bounded inspected sources.

# Theorem 1.8: additional arrangement-source candidates

Research date: 2026-11-14. Scope: exact pinned-source inspection of the two
additional repositories identified by root. Only this new report was edited.
No Lean sources, frozen reviews, configuration or provenance were changed.
No dependency was imported, built, installed, axiom-audited or kernel-replayed;
no shared cache was touched. No external supplier is accepted by this report.

## Decision

Neither candidate supplies Deligne asphericity for finite real simplicial
arrangements, a comparison of the **ordinary complex topological complement**
with a Salvetti or Deligne model, or the relative normalizer fundamental-group
identification needed in Theorem 1.8.

OrlikSolomon does have substantive, actual finite affine arrangements,
localization rings and open **scheme** complements, with explicit comparison
isomorphisms. These are not mocked topological interfaces, but their category
and topology differ from the article's `X_J^C`. Atlas's named hit is an
affine-arrangement predicate, with no complement construction or theorem.
No immediate vendoring is recommended for this theorem.

## adamtopaz/OrlikSolomon

- Repository: <https://github.com/adamtopaz/OrlikSolomon>.
- Inspected SHA: `1568c3994d24e53d39471ffe810cb076cfbccc8c`.
- Complete Git tree response: 586 entries, not truncated.
- Toolchain: `leanprover/lean4:v4.36.0-rc2`.
- Manifest mathlib: `6db5db0d2279846cc8fb25901bd53221d37a77d8`.
- Manifest Verso: `71a2035b44e7f54a797ce799fd1b03cdd3a44684`.
  The Lake configuration separates the library from the Verso book.
- License: Apache-2.0, confirmed in root LICENSE and source headers.
- Read-only source snapshot:
  `/tmp/theorem18-additional/orlik-full/OrlikSolomon-1568c3994d24e53d39471ffe810cb076cfbccc8c`.

Fetched the exact Git tree and an archive of the immutable commit. Searched
all 419 files under `OrlikSolomon/` for the relevant topology terms; inspected
the declarations and proof passages below. This is not a complete
line-by-line mathematical review of the repository.

### Real finite affine arrangements and algebraic complements

[`Geometry/Arrangement.lean`, lines 68–72](https://github.com/adamtopaz/OrlikSolomon/blob/1568c3994d24e53d39471ffe810cb076cfbccc8c/OrlikSolomon/Geometry/Arrangement.lean#L68)
defines

```lean
structure Arrangement (k : Type u) [Field k]
    (V : Type u) [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V] where
  hyperplanes : Finset (AffineSubspace k V)
  isHyperplane_of_mem' : ∀ H ∈ hyperplanes, IsHyperplane H
```

This is actual finite affine-subspace data over an arbitrary field; it can
be specialized to `ℂ`. Its restriction/deletion API uses affine pullbacks
and discards empty or full-space traces as appropriate. The definitions do
not include a real structure, chamber simpliciality, or the Euclidean
topology on the complement.

[`Geometry/Complement.lean`](https://github.com/adamtopaz/OrlikSolomon/blob/1568c3994d24e53d39471ffe810cb076cfbccc8c/OrlikSolomon/Geometry/Complement.lean)
defines `Arrangement.ComplementRing := Localization 𝒜.equationSubmonoid`.
The submonoid is generated by equations of the arrangement's hyperplanes.
This is an actual ring construction; it is explicitly **not** the type of
points in a topological complement. `ComplementRing.isLocalizationAway`
relates it to localization at a product of equations.

[`Geometry/Schemes/Complement/Basic.lean`](https://github.com/adamtopaz/OrlikSolomon/blob/1568c3994d24e53d39471ffe810cb076cfbccc8c/OrlikSolomon/Geometry/Schemes/Complement/Basic.lean)
adds actual open subschemes, in namespace `OrlikSolomon.Geometric`:

- `hyperplaneComplement H` (line 101) is the complement of the image of
  the closed immersion of the hyperplane scheme into affine space.
- `complementOpens 𝒜` (line 136) is the intersection of these open sets.
- `complement 𝒜 : Over (Spec (.of k))` (line 164) is the corresponding
  open subscheme, with its restricted structure sheaf.
- `complementIsoSpec 𝒜` (line 251) constructs an isomorphism to
  `spec (CommAlgCat.of k 𝒜.ComplementRing)`, using equality of ranges of
  actual open immersions. `complementIsoSpec_hom_comp` proves it lies over
  the ambient affine space.
- `complementMap` (line 431) constructs a scheme morphism from an affine
  map `φ : W →ᵃ[k] V` under
  `∀ K ∈ 𝒜, ℬ.Covers (K.comap φ)`. Here `Covers` means empty or a member
  of `ℬ`. `complementMap_comp_complementι` verifies the ambient square.
- `complementIso` (line 564) constructs a scheme isomorphism from an
  affine equivalence that identifies the hyperplane sets by pullback.

These are positive algebraic-geometry results. Their carriers are scheme
points with the Zariski topology, not vectors in `ℂ^n` with its usual
topology. Setting `k := ℂ` does not change this distinction. No proved
complex-points/analytification comparison to the article's topological
complement was found.

### Exact meaning of the proposed projective-complement hit

Read
[`Interface/ProjectiveComplement.lean`](https://github.com/adamtopaz/OrlikSolomon/blob/1568c3994d24e53d39471ffe810cb076cfbccc8c/OrlikSolomon/Interface/ProjectiveComplement.lean)
and the relevant definitions in `Interface/ProjectiveSpace.lean`.
`projectiveSpace k n` is `Proj` of the polynomial ring over `k`, as a
scheme over `Spec k`. In namespace `OrlikSolomon.Interface`:

- `complementOpens 𝒜` (lines 37–44) is the complement of the union of the
  projective **scheme** hyperplanes.
- `complement 𝒜` (line 49) is this open subscheme over `Spec k`.
- `complementSchemeIso` (line 113) and `complementIso` (line 129) compare
  that actual open subscheme with the library's other projective-complement
  construction. They are categorical scheme isomorphisms, not a Salvetti
  comparison or a passage to a fundamental groupoid.
- `complement_isAffine_smooth` (line 145) assumes `𝒜.Nonempty` and proves
  affineness and smoothness of the scheme complement.
- `complementIso_hom_appTop_projectiveRatio` and `isUnit_ratio` compare
  global sections and prove invertibility of ratios of hyperplane equations.

The statements quantify over arbitrary fields and projective dimensions.
They contain no simplicial-arrangement hypothesis and no homotopy,
asphericity, covering-space or normalizer conclusion. In particular,
`complementIso` does not fill any of the topological comparison gaps in
the Theorem 1.8 source inventory.

### Cohomology examples and absence of a formal singular bridge

Read the relevant sections of
[`Examples/ProjectiveOrdinary.lean`](https://github.com/adamtopaz/OrlikSolomon/blob/1568c3994d24e53d39471ffe810cb076cfbccc8c/OrlikSolomon/Examples/ProjectiveOrdinary.lean).
`singleHyperplaneCohomologyEquiv`, `nonempty_basis_points_grading_one`, and
related declarations take a supplied `T : OrdinaryTheory ...`. The explicit
three-point finite-field examples include the zero coefficient theory.
These test the specified cohomology interface and its edge cases; they are
not proofs about classical `π₁` or `K(π,1)` spaces. The final interface
examples test actual affine/smooth scheme complements and equation ratios.

[`Cohomology/Axioms.lean`, immediately before `OrdinaryTheory`](https://github.com/adamtopaz/OrlikSolomon/blob/1568c3994d24e53d39471ffe810cb076cfbccc8c/OrlikSolomon/Cohomology/Axioms.lean#L118)
explicitly states:

> “This is a mathematical argument, not a formal one: no singular instance
> exists in Lean, so a statement about singular cohomology still needs a
> value of this structure for it.”

The same passage distinguishes the constructed nonzero characteristic-zero
algebraic de Rham instance from the zero theories. I do not characterize
the whole cohomology development as vacuous: the relevant limit is that
neither algebraic de Rham cohomology nor a conditional ordinary-theory
isomorphism supplies the required topological asphericity or relative
fundamental-group equivalence.

### Verification and reading limits

The calculated `OrlikSolomon.*` source import closure of
`Interface.ProjectiveComplement` contains 22 modules, 11,052 source lines,
all present, with remaining imports in mathlib. A source screen found no
`sorry`, `admit`, custom `axiom` declaration, `unsafe def/theorem`, or
`opaque` declaration in that closure. This is not a transitive axiom audit.
The temporary list is
`/tmp/theorem18-additional/orlik-projective-interface-closure.txt`.

Read the audit tool's introductory design and the replay script. They
describe private-level import inspection, checking all project declarations
against the three usual axioms, and per-module kernel replay. Their source
and README claims do not establish that any such checks were run here.
No build, fresh audit or replay was performed by this task.

Full-source term searches under `OrlikSolomon/` found no occurrence of
`Deligne`, `Salvetti`, `asphericity`, `aspherical`, `SimplyConnectedSpace`,
`FundamentalGroup`, `HomotopyGroup`, `ComplexManifold`, `Analytification`,
or `SingularCohomology`. This is bounded textual evidence, not a proof that
every equivalent formulation is absent. The explicitly documented missing
singular instance and the inspected exact statement types are stronger
evidence for rejecting the proposed topological use.

## facebookresearch/atlas-lean

- Repository: <https://github.com/facebookresearch/atlas-lean>.
- Inspected SHA: `8e813e63090880e090494edfb55c7602cd961987`.
- Complete Git tree response: 24,571 entries, not truncated.
- Toolchain: Lean `v4.35.0`.
- Manifest mathlib: `56a005855ea17e0b0958f73ec801ae140b0a1679`.
- Root LICENSE contains Apache-2.0 text, preceded by the repository's
  statement that the codebase is not intended for ML-model development.
  No code was copied or proposed for reuse.

Read the full
[`MathlibExt/Combinatorics/Poset/Basic.lean`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/atlas-lean/blob/8e813e63090880e090494edfb55c7602cd961987/MathlibExt/Combinatorics/Poset/Basic.lean).
Its only arrangement declaration is in namespace `MetaMathlibExt`, line 230:

```lean
def IsHyperplaneArrangement {K V : Type*} [Field K]
    [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] [FiniteDimensional K V]
    (E : AffineSubspace K V) (A : Set (AffineSubspace K V)) : Prop :=
  A.Finite ∧ ∀ H ∈ A, H ≤ E ∧ (H : Set V).Nonempty ∧
    Module.finrank K H.direction + 1 =
      Module.finrank K E.direction
```

This is a faithful finite codimension-one affine-arrangement predicate.
The module's other definitions are Möbius multiplication and flag
vectors. It provides no complement, continuous map, groupoid, or theorem
about arrangements, and therefore no direct missing proof supplier.

Also read
[`MathlibExt/AlgebraicGeometry/LineArrangement.lean`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/atlas-lean/blob/8e813e63090880e090494edfb55c7602cd961987/MathlibExt/AlgebraicGeometry/LineArrangement.lean).
It defines finite projective-plane line sets, multiplicities, pairwise
intersection points and their Harbourne constant; its substantive results
identify singular points and show their existence. These concern incidence
and counting, not complement topology.

Searched the complete pinned tree's path inventory for arrangement,
complement, Salvetti, Deligne and asphericity candidates. I did not download
or text-search every Atlas source file, audit its transitive definitions,
or inspect its unrelated `WantedExt` and historical `v1` mathematics.
No broad code-search queries were used, and none of the negative result
depends on a rate-limited search response.

## Remaining obligations and disposition

Neither source changes the missing bridges recorded in `search-openai.md`:
the actual relative complex complement; the finite simplicial arrangement
and normalizer action; a verified comparison to its own topological
Salvetti/Deligne model; asphericity; the ribbon/normalizer vertex-group
identification; and compatibility of all covering and algebraic exact
sequence maps, including basepoints and path-composition conventions.

The OrlikSolomon affine restriction API could be reconsidered if the
project later needs algebraic arrangement incidence or coordinate-ring
theorems. That possibility alone does not justify adding its dependency
closure to this topological proof. Atlas's predicate is only a definition,
not a proof of an outstanding prerequisite.

No mathematical error in either inspected source or the original article
was established. A category/topology mismatch and an explicitly unformalized
comparison are reuse limitations, not allegations of false statements.

# Theorem 1.8: openai/math and revised source search

Research date: 2026-11-14. This is a source-inspection report, not a proof
acceptance or a claim that Theorem 1.8 has been formalized. Read the dedicated
repository's README, MIGRATION and ARTICLE-DEPENDENCIES before this search.
No proof package, earlier record, toolchain or shared cache was modified.

## Result

No directly applicable formal supplier for the **relative hyperplane
complement** in Theorem 1.8 was found in the inspected sources. Both
repositories contain a substantial ordinary Artin Salvetti development,
including a stated contractible universal cover and a fundamental-group
isomorphism for its combinatorial quotient. They do not provide the needed
comparison with the article's relative complexified arrangement complement,
the action of `N(W,J)` on that complement, or the compatible normalizer
fundamental-group exact sequence.

The combinatorial Salvetti definitions are substantive: the base space is
constructed by gluing actual spherical Coxeter permutahedra. I found no
definition replacing the target space by a point, and no conclusion is
merely assumed as a field in the inspected endpoint definitions. This does
**not** establish the validity of the entire 617-module proof closure.
No candidate was compiled, transitively axiom-audited, or kernel-replayed in
this search; none is accepted as verified for reuse.

## Target checked against the article

Read Theorem 1.8, the introduction's description of its groupoid proof,
equation (3.26), Theorem 6.7 and its proof, Remark 6.12, and Corollary 6.14
and its proof in the local PDF of arXiv:2509.21915v3.

The actual space in (3.26), PDF page 13, is

```text
X_J^C = (Cone(J)° × Cone(J)°) \ ⋃_{H∈H_J} (H × H).
```

Under sphericality, the relative arrangement is a finite central real
arrangement with open simplicial chambers. Corollary 6.14 invokes Deligne's
theorem for such arrangements. It does not assert that the relative
arrangement is itself the Coxeter arrangement of a new Coxeter matrix.
Theorem 6.7 identifies the normal-cover exact sequence with the algebraic
normalizer sequence through the Deligne groupoid, its `N(W,J)` quotient,
and the reduced ribbon groupoid. Remark 3.25, PDF page 12, explicitly
states that the `N(W,J)` action need not be chamber-transitive.

Consequently, an ordinary Coxeter–Salvetti theorem cannot be applied just
by choosing another matrix `M`. The relevant arrangement, its comparison
maps and equivariance must first be proved. No replacement of `X_J^C` by a
classifying-space model is authorized by this report.

## Immutable sources and coverage

| Repository | Inspected commit |
| --- | --- |
| <https://github.com/openai/math> | `4eaee87548250b2682affda7d05d947c05554bae` |
| <https://github.com/mathcommunity/oai-math-revised> | `d25fae85c2f5ce5aadac40fb2b4c2d332b393d1c` |

Both commits specify Lean `v4.34.1`, mathlib
`d13f23b723b8a846827a245b89c10fc7d3f11612`, and Apache-2.0 licensing.
The package's `lakefile.lean` additionally requires numerous external
projects, including a TauCeti revision; importing the whole repository is
not justified by the source search.
